articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft Prospects to Watch in Week 6
articles.summary: As we approach the mid-season point, we can tick another group of prospects off the list of those yet to be tested. Georgia travels to Alabama in the big gam...
articles.body:
As we approach the mid-season point, we can tick another group of prospects off the list of those yet to be tested. Georgia travels to Alabama in the big game of Week 6. Who should you watch in this one, and the other big NFL Draft matchups of Week 6?

2027 NFL Draft Prospects to Watch in Week 6

Matchup of the Week – Georgia at Alabama (7:30 p.m. ET, ABC)

This game has not only been a high-stakes SEC rivalry, it's also been a marquee game for an array of NFL Draft prospects over the years. You can be sure a large number of NFL scouts will be in attendance.

The best pure matchup of NFL Draft prospects in this one is Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams against a Georgia secondary featuring cornerback Ellis Robinson IV and safety K.J. Bolden. Coleman-Williams dropped far too many passes in 2025 (even while wearing a knee brace last week against Mississippi State), but appears to have eradicated them from his game. Can he keep this up in a high-pressure game?

Alabama edge Yhonzae Pierre was quiet last week against Mississippi State. Given the Dylan Stewart situation is cloudy right now, there could be an opportunity to be the second Edge draft behind Colin Simmons (Texas). This is the perfect platform to push those claims.

The off-ball linebacker class this year is strong. The NFL doesn't necessarily value the position on draft day, but there are impact prospects in this class. Having said that, Georgia's Chris Cole is doing everything he can to push for the first round. Can that continue in this environment against a physical opponent ?

2027 NFL Draft Prospects to Watch in Week 5 – Friday Night Lights (All Times Eastern)

Friday night is a busy one with five games. The main focus with Florida State seems to be whether or not donors are willing to buy out Mike Norvell's contract. They do have an interesting receiving prospect in Duce Robinson, a big target playing the "X" position, as they visit Louisville (7:00 p.m., ESPN).

Louisville edge rusher Clev Lubin has enjoyed a number of good matchups so far this season, and gets another chance to impress. More scouts are likely to attend a Friday night game, so it's a good stage as he looks to cement a top 50 slot.

These Friday night matchups offer the chance to watch prospects who may not be top 100 prospects, but can still make an NFL roster. Washington offensive tackle Drew Azzopardi is one such prospect, as they take on Iowa (9:00 p.m., Fox). It will be interesting to stack him against last week's Friday night offensive tackle, Pitt's Ryan Baer.

Iowa was humbled by Ohio State last week, so it's a short turnaround while licking its wounds. It will be interesting to see how their trio of potential top 100 picks respond (offensive tackle Trevor Lauck, guard Kade Pieper and safety Zach Lutmer).

One other game would have featured a rising prospect, but injury looks like it will get in the way in Iowa State's visit to Brigham Young (10:15 p.m., ESPN). Unfortunately, per the Salt Lake Tribune , Brigham Young running back LJ Martin is doubtful with a lower leg injury.

Other 2027 NFL Draft Prospects to Watch in Week 6 (All Times Eastern)

After the vicious hit he took against Southern California, hopefully Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will start against UCLA (3:30 p.m., CBS). Thankfully, the injury is just a concussion, and as Yahoo Sports is reporting , Moore is back in practice.

UCLA has started the season well and has two rising prospects who will be tested against a top team. Running back Wayne Knight is tiny (5'7", 193 lbs) but electric. If his athletic ability stands out against a defense like Oregon's, NFL teams may well look to ignore the lack of size.

Also for UCLA, linebacker Sammy Omosigho has been a tackling machine; he also has four forced fumbles. The Oregon offensive line is a good one (led by center Iapani Laloulu), so the matchup is an interesting one.

The annual Red River Rivalry (3:30 p.m., ABC) is a chance to see a defensive tackle prospect who it was feared was done for the year. Oklahoma's David Stone dislocated a kneecap in practice, but played against Georgia just over a week later. Watching him will involve seeing how healthy he looks first, before deciding whether or not to include the performance as part of his evaluation.

The big question for Texas quarterback Arch Manning is: can he string together four strong quarters? Then he needs to string together games where he does this. He's a rhythm passer, but he must find a way to be more consistent.

While Arkansas might be struggling again in the SEC, they do still have NFL prospects; a rising prospect is Boise State transfer Chris Marshall. The receiver has 35 catches already this year, and he will be tested against Tennessee (4:15 p.m., SEC Network).

2027 NFL Draft Prospects to Watch in Week 6 – Small Schools

The feature game with NFL Draft prospects on both teams is Montana at Northern Arizona (5:00 p.m., ESPN+). Montana running back Eli Gillman is an explosive back who needs to continue to work on his pass protection. Northern Arizona quarterback Ty Pennington will be tested against a long-time FCS powerhouse.

North Dakota offensive tackle Trace Thaden is a Shrine Bowl 1,000 Watch List prospect who was highly regarded coming into the season . He faces a road test at Northern Iowa (5:00 p.m., ESPN+).

There's no question that pre-season NFL Draft boards are already looking dated. There will be more change in the coming weeks, with injuries playing a part in the ever-shifting NFL Draft picture.

The consensus preseason top-rated quarterback this year, Arch Manning, is under constant scrutiny. He has yet to play like an elite prospect, with a lack of consistency becoming a major concern. He must find it for Texas if he wishes to declare for the 2027 NFL Draft.

The Georgia/Alabama game will draw the most NFL scouts this week. Coleman-Williams has the potential to be the highest-drafted prospect on show, particularly if he continues to avoid the drops that plagued his 2025 season.

Two highly rated prospects are worth monitoring health-wise this week. Moore and Stone suffered nasty-sounding injuries, but thankfully seem to be back on track.

Keep an eye out for rising UCLA running back Wayne Knight. The James Madison transfer is electric and a highlight waiting to happen.

articles.body: Travis Kelce, the 37 year old Kansas City Chiefs’ popular tight end, has had a record breaking performance in the new season even though many had doubted if he was fit enough to play this time. While he gears up for the Week 5 clash, Travis Kelce opened up about making a meaningful impact through his foundation, 87 & Running.Travis Kelce reflects on how his foundation 87 and Running has helped change lives in Kansas CityIn an episode on ESPN’s show, Chiefs Kingdom, the popular tight end Travis Kelce opened up about his collaboration with Kansas City’s Operation Breakthrough as he said, "one of the coolest places that I've ever seen or been a part of…”The 11 time Pro Bowler added, "They literally have kids from preschool all the way to 8th grade, and they’re making sure these kids have meals, a safe haven; they get their education, they have good guidance and mentors…”The star tight end added, "It was beautiful to see what that organization was doing for those kids," Kelce continued. "And it was a little unsettling at the end when I found out that the program stopped at eighth grade."Travis Kelce also reflected on the importance of having a support system around him while growing up as he said, "were such a big part of my development and who I am as a person. I was so fortunate that I had the people around me and the environment around me to make sure I was doing the right things," he added.Travis Kelce’s foundation 87 and Running finds itself in controversial news as he keeps himself distant from itWhile Travis Kelce’s foundation has brought in many changes in Kansas City, it has also found itself in a mess considering the controversial headlines in the last few months.Earlier in this year, the 11 time Pro Bowler Travis Kelce’s foundation found itself amid money laundering claims as reports hinted that out of $1.5 million raised, nearly $470,000 went toward high management and general expenses rather than charitable work.Despite the controversial nature of the news, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce has kept himself away from all the negative news as he remains focused on the field.During the offseason, Travis Kelce dealt with all the buzz about his personal life as many claimed that he has grown unfit due to his wedding and should just retire.But the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end remained focused on the field and has bounced back on the field with a record breaking performance in the new season.Travis Kelce has continued his work at 87 and Running despite the negativity surrounding it.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Jason Kelce, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star player, has turned into a pretty successful entrepreneur after his retirement from the league. Jason Kelce has started a number of ventures in the last few years alongside his younger brother, Travis Kelce, but he has always remained committed to giving back to the society and his wife, Kylie Kelce, has stood by his side through it.Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, give back to Philadelphia as they stand by the cityA few weeks ago, the NFL icon Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, held the sixth annual Team 62 at the Ocean Drive fundraiser raising a record breaking $1.26 million for the Eagles Autism Foundation.The special event was held at Ocean Drive in Sea Isle City and had many of the current and former Eagles stars who acted as "celebrity bartenders” at the event.In a statement, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ star Jason Kelce and his wife, popular podcaster Kylie Kelce, said, "We are beyond thankful for everyone's support and generosity in setting a Team 62 fundraising record…While we are certainly humbled by the overwhelming success this year, it's not surprising when you're surrounded by such an incredible group of people.”Jason Kelce and his wife, Kylie Kelce, added, “The growth of this event all starts with our good friends at the OD for enthusiastically leaning into this idea of ours back in 2021. articles.title: “Satan hates seeing Christian people marry”: Chiefs billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt opens up on the role of faith in her wedding
articles.summary: Gracie Hunt, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress has been a pretty strong support to the team as she remains focused on being there for the team.
articles.body: Gracie Hunt, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress has been a pretty strong support to the team as she remains focused on being there for the team. Alongside the new season, Gracie Hunt has also been planning her high profile wedding to fiance, Derek Green, and she has opened up about how important her faith has been in the process.Chiefs’ billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt opens up on how her faith is the most important thing in her wedding planning processA few weeks ago, on The Riley Gaines Show, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt said, "We did marriage counseling before we ever got engaged…I just think it's a really good way to know if you are ready for marriage, and it also takes the pressure off because I think once you become engaged in today's day and age it's difficult to do that afterwards…”Gracie Hunt added, “I actually think it's a really healthy thing to do when you are deciding, 'Okay, is this my person? And so if you're someone who's thinking about getting engaged, I would encourage doing that…”The popular investor continued, "Since then, you know, we're really involved in our church and in Bible study. We're working with some pastors and doing some premarital counseling, some extra premarital counseling just to make sure that we're really poured into and solid during this time of life because I also think, and this is a little bit of a hot take, once you become engaged, I think that Satan hates seeing Christian people marry Christian people.”The billionaire heiress added, “And I think that it's a very vulnerable time in a relationship. There's a lot more pressure… I think that you just have to constantly pray over your relationship and for protection. And that the Lord would sustain you both and bring you closer to each other and to him."Over the last few years, in many of her interviews, the Kansas City Chiefs’ billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt has often sparked a debate among many with her comments on religion but she has remained focused on being dedicated to her faith.Gracie Hunt focuses on her wedding to Derek Green amid an impressive seasonIn the last few months, after getting engaged to her fiance Derek Green, the son of Kansas City Chiefs’ legend Trent Green, Gracie Hunt has often spoken about how she was always meant to be with him.The two met in their childhood and drifted apart only to become friends in 2017 again.Gracie Hunt and Derek Green went public with their relationship last year and earlier this year, he proposed to her and the two got engaged.Amid the unbeatable season of the Kansas City Chiefs, Gracie Hunt also remains busy planning her wedding.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Charlotte Tilbury is taking its relationship with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders into another season, combining beauty, performance and retail in a partnership built around the group’s signature game-day looks. The beauty brand will remain the team’s official beauty partner for a second year, while its expanded Amazon Beauty collaboration will give shoppers more ways to discover and buy the products used behind the scenes.Charlotte Tilbury becomes Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ beauty partner for second yearThe renewed partnership goes beyond makeup. Charlotte Tilbury will support the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders through content, creator experiences, retail appearances and in-stadium activations. The brand will also help create the team’s official beauty looks for game days.For the 2026 collaboration, Charlotte Tilbury has put together a beauty wardrobe designed around the demanding routines of the cheerleaders. The collection brings together skin care, complexion products and colour cosmetics, giving the team a full routine rather than relying on a single signature product.The skin care line-up includes Magic Cream, Magic Serum Crystal Elixir, Hollywood Skin Secrets Immediate Eye Revival Patches and Invisible UV Flawless Primer SPF 50. The complexion range includes Airbrush Flawless Foundation, Airbrush Flawless Blur Concealer, Airbrush Flawless Finish, Airbrush Flawless Blur Loose Powder and Airbrush Flawless Setting Spray.The wider makeup collection features products such as Hollywood Contour Wand, Airbrush Bronzer, Beauty Light Wands, Exagger-Eyes Volume Mascara, Legendary Brows and Pillow Talk lip products.Kelli Finglass, senior director of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, highlighted the confidence element behind the partnership."Looking good makes you feel good and feeling good gives you confidence," said Kelli Finglass, senior director of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders. "That's what we love about Charlotte Tilbury. It's a brand that's really about confidence and helping women feel their best. For the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, that confidence is so important because when they feel good about themselves, they can step out on the field and perform at their very best."Charlotte Tilbury expands Amazon Beauty partnershipThe collaboration also creates a stronger link between the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ beauty routines and online shopping. Charlotte Tilbury is expanding its Amazon Beauty retail partnership with new ways for customers to explore the products featured in the team’s looks.The strategy gives the partnership a digital layer, allowing fans and beauty shoppers to move from behind-the-scenes content to the products themselves. Exclusive experiences and retail activations are also expected to bring consumers closer to the cheerleaders’ preparation process.Camille Nordby, Premium Beauty Category Leader at Amazon U.S. Stores, said the partnership can help customers connect with the products in a more engaging way."We couldn't be more proud of Amazon Beauty's collaboration with Charlotte Tilbury Beauty," said Camille Nordby, Premium Beauty Category Leader, Amazon U.S. Stores. "Charlotte Tilbury is a brand built on confidence, artistry, and showing up as your best self. We can't wait to bring customers closer to the action with behind-the-scenes content, exclusive experiences, and the products behind the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' iconic looks."With beauty routines now playing a larger role in fan and retail experiences, the renewed partnership positions Charlotte Tilbury at the centre of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ 2026 season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady’s $100,000 donation sparked wider relief push as GoPuff matched contributions up to $1 million
articles.summary: In 2024, Tom Brady used his platform to support Floridians facing the aftermath of Hurricane Milton, making a $100,000 donation toward disaster relief.
articles.body: In 2024, Tom Brady used his platform to support Floridians facing the aftermath of Hurricane Milton, making a $100,000 donation toward disaster relief. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback also helped encourage others to contribute by highlighting a matching programme from GoPuff. The initiative aimed to get basic supplies into the hands of people dealing with the storm’s immediate impact, while supporting broader recovery efforts across Florida.Tom Brady donates $100,000 to Hurricane Milton reliefBrady announced his contribution shortly after Hurricane Milton struck Florida as a powerful Category 3 storm. The hurricane brought dangerous winds, storm surge and heavy rain, while tornadoes added another layer of risk across parts of the state.The storm left millions of customers without electricity and caused widespread damage. With communities facing urgent shortages, Brady focused his donation on practical necessities rather than simply offering public support."In the wake of Hurricane Milton, I'll be making a donation of $100k to help get essentials like food, water and first aid to fellow Floridians in need," Brady posted on X.His contribution also opened the door for people who wanted to help but could only give smaller amounts. GoPuff, which had partnered with Brady earlier that year, agreed to match donations made through its Give With Gopuff programme."My friends at @gopuff are matching this, along with all other donations made via 'Give With Gopuff', all benefiting the Volunteer Florida Foundation," Brady said. "Keep those impacted by these storms in your prayers, look out for your neighbors, and continue to help out anyway you're able. Stay safe, and stay strong Florida."GoPuff and Taylor Swift support hurricane victimsThe GoPuff campaign gave users a direct way to donate everyday essentials through the company's app. For each eligible item donated through the Give With Gopuff collection, the company pledged to match the contribution and send the products to the Volunteer Florida Foundation, up to $1 million.GoPuff also committed additional bulk donations through the Florida Disaster Fund to help supply relief centres across the state.Brady was not the only major name to step forward after Milton. Taylor Swift also announced a significant contribution to hurricane recovery efforts. Feeding America said the singer donated $5 million to support people affected by Hurricanes Helene and Milton."We’re incredibly grateful to Taylor Swift for her generous $5 million donation to Hurricanes Helene and Milton relief efforts,” Feeding America's CEO Claire Babineaux-Fontenot wrote. “This contribution will help communities rebuild and recover, providing essential food, clean water, and supplies to people affected by these devastating storms."Together, the donations from Brady, Swift and other contributors highlighted the scale of the response needed as Florida communities began the difficult process of recovery.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio estate faces growing neighbor dispute over $75,000 sewer issue
articles.summary: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s new Ohio property has become the centre of a growing dispute, with neighbors raising concerns about plans to improve
articles.body: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s new Ohio property has become the centre of a growing dispute, with neighbors raising concerns about plans to improve privacy around the sprawling lakefront estate. What began as a disagreement over fencing and landscaping has expanded into a much wider clash involving wildlife, security, access and an ageing sewer line shared with a nearby home. Local residents say they fear the proposed changes could create problems long after the couple’s plans for the property are complete.Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion sparks concerns over fence and landscapingThe $5.35 million estate in Bratenahl, near Cleveland, has drawn attention since Kelce bought it through an LLC earlier this year. The 21,000-square-foot property includes eight bedrooms, 11 bathrooms and a guest cottage overlooking Lake Erie.At a recent Architectural Review Board meeting, neighbors questioned the couple’s plans for a six-foot black aluminium fence and extensive landscaping. One resident, Katherine Bolton, focused on an old clay sewer pipe shared by the neighboring properties.She claimed planting dozens of evergreen trees close to the line could allow roots to damage the ageing pipe. Bolton said she had been quoted $75,000 to reinforce it against possible root intrusion.“Planting 50 evergreen trees just ten feet from a 100-year-old clay sewer line is virtually guaranteed to cause severe root intrusion, pipe structural failure and catastrophic sewage backups,” Bolton told the meeting, citing research she conducted using artificial intelligence.The concerns highlight a difficult balance between the privacy expected at a celebrity-owned property and the practical needs of longtime residents.Neighbors raise security and wildlife concernsOther objections centred on the fence itself. Neighbor Chuck Bauernschmidt questioned whether its pointed design could pose a danger to deer moving through the area. Village official Mary Ranney acknowledged that deer can occasionally become caught on fence points.Security also became part of the discussion. Bill Bolton, Katherine’s husband and a former village council president, argued that a fence alone would not necessarily stop determined intruders or paparazzi.“I think that the greater security threat for the applicant is from drones and the water,” he said, urging the village to consider those risks.The couple’s construction team said they had already made several compromises. The original proposal called for an eight-foot fence stretching around much of the property. The final plan reduced its height, moved it further inside the boundary and stopped it short of the lake.Their team also said $7,500 had been spent repairing part of the shared sewer and that the line had been cleaned.For now, the landscaping dispute remains unresolved. Some planting plans were approved with conditions, while a proposed shoreline screen was rejected, meaning another review will be required before the work can move ahead.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Taking The L: What We've Been The Most Wrong About Through 1st Quarter Of NFL Season
articles.summary: We're eating a slice of humble pie and sharing which of our preseason predictions were the most off-base.
articles.body: The first four weeks of the 2026 NFL season were far from predictable. A sliver of teams with playoff (and even championship) hopes are winless. The Minnesota Vikings are one of the final three undefeated teams left. Kenneth Walker III looks like the favorite to win Offensive Player of the Year, and the Los Angeles Rams haven't been as invincible as we thought they might be. We technically aren't at the exact quarter mark of the 2026 NFL season, but we're just about there. So, as we prepare for Week 5, we're taking a look back on some of our preseason predictions and eating a slice of humble pie as we share what we were wrong about the most. Justin Herbert's Poor Play Ralph Vacchiano: I have been high on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert since 2019, when the New York Giants desperately hoped he’d come out for the draft, one year before he actually did. I thought he had everything I’d want in an NFL quarterback, and I blamed his teammates, coaches and his dysfunctional franchise for why he hasn’t already won multiple Super Bowl trophies and MVPs. This year, though, I thought everything was set up for him. I believed Jim Harbaugh made a brilliant move to bring in Mike McDaniel to work his wizardry at offensive coordinator. I thought they fixed their line, too. By the end of this season, I was sure Herbert and the Chargers would emerge as a sleeper Super Bowl threat. Um, about that … They’re obviously 0-4, possibly headed towards 0-9 if you look at their schedule, and McDaniel and Herbert look like they’re reading the same book in different languages. There is no cohesion on offense, no answers from the coaches, and all seems lost. Just a month ago, 10 wins and the playoffs seemed like the floor for this team. I believed that Herbert, who has been floundering the last three seasons, would finally be back on his Hall of Fame track. Now, all I can do is accept that Herbert might be the most overrated quarterback of this generation. I still think the talent is there. But his potential may forever go unfulfilled. Texans Far From Super Bowl Contention Ben Arthur: The Texans were an easy Super Bowl pick for me ahead of the season. Their all-world defense from a year ago lost no significant contributors over the offseason; they arguably got even better (added free-agent safety Reed Blakenship, second-round rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald). And I couldn’t imagine quarterback C.J. Stroud playing worse than he did in the playoffs last season, when he had seven turnovers in two games. If Stroud could keep Houston’s offense on schedule and the defense kept doing its thing, the Texans had a championship formula. So it’s been bizarre to see Stroud and the Texans’ defense essentially switch places in their stunning 0-4 start: the quarterback play has been fine — great at times — but the defense has regressed dramatically. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed and 26th in points allowed through four games. The team has been particularly bad defending the pass, ranking 28th with 260.0 passing yards allowed per game. Stroud has shown very real signs of growth, and I think the defense will be fine after head coach DeMeco Ryans took back defensive play-calling responsibilities this week. But I think the hole they’ve dug for themselves is too big to overcome. The Jaguars are positioned to run away with the AFC South, and there will be some very good teams fighting for the three wild-card spots in the AFC. Jim Harbaugh-Mike McDaniel Pairing Has Been A Disaster Eric D. Williams: I thought the unusual pairing between the old-school approach of veteran head coach Jim Harbaugh and the new-school approach of quirky offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel would work, despite their differing personalities. Instead, through the first four weeks, it’s been an ineffective combo, with Harbaugh having to answer questions about firing his offensive coordinator. The uber-talented Justin Herbert is playing his worst football in his seven-year NFL career. L.A.’s offense looks disjointed, riddled with miscues and sloppy penalties. The Chargers are hampered by injuries again, with four of the team’s projected starting five along the offensive line already suffering injuries that forced them to miss time. The Chargers have one of the worst scoring offenses in the league, and there’s no sign that things will turn around soon, with one of the best defenses in the league traveling to SoFi Stadium to face the Bolts in the Denver Broncos. Once again, the Chargers appear to be facing another lost season led by one of the most talented quarterbacks in the league, and at the center of that struggle is the strained relationship between Harbaugh, McDaniel and Herbert. The Pleasant Surprises Greg Auman: I took the Chargers to win the Super Bowl and thought highly of the Texans, so it would be easy to echo the shock of those two teams opening to 0-4 records. I’ll pivot to the other side of surprise, and three current playoff teams I didn’t see coming: the Giants, Raiders and Browns, all off to promising 3-1 starts. You never know how quickly a new coach can imprint on a team that has struggled, and Klint Kubiak has certainly impressed in his first month in Las Vegas. Kubiak had bounced to five teams in five years before winning a Super Bowl last year, from the Vikings to Broncos to 49ers to Chiefs to Seahawks. He looks like someone who has learned from every stop and knows how to build a winning culture. General manager John Spytek spent big in free agency, but Tyler Linderbaum looks like a game-changer, and Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker are a great young linebacker duo. It may not translate to the playoffs this year, but the trajectory is undeniably upward. There’s so much less standing between the Giants and a division title in John Harbaugh’s first season there. The Eagles are now down three solid offensive linemen, and the Cowboys show little sign that their defense isn’t the limiting factor it was last year. Can Jameis Winston play a full season without falling back to old turnover habits? That may be the biggest question, but New York’s defensive front and rookie linebacker Arvell Reese should only improve as the year progresses. And Cleveland, off to a 3-1 start with their only loss at Jacksonville? Todd Monken is the old man in this first-year head coach class, and he’s managed to win with Deshaun Watson, a wrinkle nobody saw coming. Rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are playmakers, and second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham had four sacks in his first three games before falling to injury. Their schedule is loaded with winnable games, and while they’re unlikely to catch Baltimore, they could stick around in an AFC North where all four teams are at .500 or better right now. Cowboys' Defense Failing To Meet Expectations Steven Ruiz: I’ll go with the idea that the Cowboys' defense can be "average." I really bought into it and picked Dallas to win the NFC East. My optimism was based on new defensive coordinator Christian Parker, but I’m already selling my stock. It’s early, so Parker could develop into a great play-caller someday, but Dallas's defense isn't playing like a well-coached unit right now. There have been coverage busts, missed tackles, and blown assignments all over the field. So, it feels an awful lot like the 2025 version of the defense. I’m sure some of that will get resolved over the next few months, but it’s going to be difficult to fix all of it. Thursday's upset loss to the Buccaneers further increased my concern surrounding the Cowboys' defense. The Cowboys are on pace to give up their second-most rushing yards in franchise history, with Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving rushing for a career-high 165 rushing yards. Beyond the coaching issues, there’s still a concerning lack of talent. I’d hoped the safeties would improve with the addition of first-round pick Caleb Downs, but the rookie has mostly been used as a nickel back, leaving Markquese Bell and Malik Hooker to cover the deep parts of the field. They’ve been a disaster, and it’s tanked the entire pass unit. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s arrival could push Downs back to safety, patching one of the biggest holes on that unit. But as the defense is currently constructed, this is far from a playoff-level unit. With Philadelphia’s season in peril and New York rolling with Jameis Winston for the foreseeable future, the bar for this defense to win the division is much lower than I expected in the offseason. So my take on the defense may have been irredeemably wrong, but I’m still feeling good about my NFC East pick. The Chiefs Are Actually Playoff-Bound Henry McKenna: I thought the Chiefs would miss the playoffs, and that was because I thought Patrick Mahomes would need some time before getting on the field — let alone looking like a top-three quarterback. I also thought Kenneth Walker III wouldn’t magically transform the Chiefs’ offensive identity. I was skeptical of whether bringing back OC Eric Bieniemy was the right move — when the team needed fresh ideas. I was beginning to think that maybe there wasn’t enough talent on defense, even with Steve Spagnuolo pulling the strings. So, yeah, I got all that wrong. Every single element. After just four games, the Chiefs have an 89% chance at making the playoffs, tied for the highest in the NFL. They have the highest odds to get the AFC’s No. 1 seed. That’s because Mahomes is playing the best football he’s played in the last five years. Walker looks like he’s on the same play-making plane as the likes of Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs. Bieniemy and Andy Reid have used Walker to bring new life to a dud of an offense. And Spags looks just fine working with the guys he’s got, including high-impact rookies Mansoor Delane, the team’s new CB1, and R Mason Thomas, the team’s rotational edge rusher. The Chiefs took a number of calculated risks. Every single one has paid off. The dynasty is alive and well. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: 'Football 301' on 49ers vs. Seahawks: Brock Purdy and his offensive machine face their biggest test
articles.summary: How will the chess match between Kyle Shanahan's 49ers offense and Mike Macdonald's Seahawks defense play out in this titanic early-season tilt?
articles.body:
It's not every day you see a Week 5 matchup as impactful as this week's NFC West clash between the San Francisco 49ers (4-0) and Seattle Seahawks (3-1) on Sunday afternoon in Seattle. With NFC playoff implications and a long-standing rivalry at stake, the stage is set for what Yahoo Sports NFL analyst Nate Tice aptly dubbed the "Hoss Fight of the Week." Tice and fellow Yahoo analyst Matt Harmon discussed the matchup on this week's episode of the " Football 301" podcast and how they expect the game to play out Sunday.

Game of adjustments: 49ers offense vs. Seahawks defense

Coming into this game, the 49ers' offense has looked untouchable. Tice said San Francisco "is tipping the scales in every single stat." The Niners haven't allowed a sack all season, a feat that seems almost fictional in today's NFL. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has his offensive machine humming, QB Brock Purdy is leading the way as "the dot at the top right of every chart right now" thanks to scorching-hot efficiency and command.

The chess match between Shanahan and Seattle head coach Mike Macdonald is a heavyweight bout. Seattle's defense, loaded up front, will look to feast if the 49ers stick to what was comfortable. The Niners, meanwhile, might look to stress the boundaries with hard play-action and hope for chunk gains, but Seattle's back end has proven tough.

As Harmon pointed out, San Francisco's lack of elite wide receiver depth could show in this matchup as George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey have carried much of the load this season.

Harmon also highlighted San Francisco's tendency to "get away with it," using its creative playbook to mitigate a lack of star power on the outside. But this, he said, was a week where even the best schemers will be tested by top-level athletes and disciplined execution.

Harmon confidently predicted: "I feel like this is the week that the no sacks taken streak gets broken." Why? The Seahawks' defense is starting to find its groove, especially in the trenches, and this would be the toughest front the Niners have faced this season.

The Seahawks have been one of the league's best against the run, ranking third in running back stuff rate and allowing just 0.5 yards before contact on running back carries. Explosive runs? Nearly non-existent. Pass defense? Even better — only eight explosive passes allowed all season compared to the league average of 18.

The Niners' renowned ground game will be tested, especially with Kyle Juszczyk expected to be out with a knee injury. Tice wonders how Shanahan might adapt, given that Seattle has devoured zone runs this season, allowing just two explosive plays and leading in stuffs against zone concepts. But gap and duo runs offered a glimmer of hope, as Seattle was only average against duo.

A critical subplot involved the Seahawks' near-total embrace of zone coverage: "90% zone rate on all downs, 90% on late downs — the lowest rate of Cover 1 in history," noted Tice. If there's an edge for Shanahan, it might be in leaning on play-action away from those cloud corners, as the Chargers managed a few times.

Can Seattle get its struggling run game off the ground?

Harmon dubbed the Seahawks' run offense vs. the 49ers' run defense "movable object versus a stoppable force" as both units have struggled this year. The Seahawks have cycled through running backs with injuries to Zach Charbonnet and George Holani. Emanuel Wilson had flashed some effectiveness, but the team has largely languished near the bottom of the league in efficiency stats.

Seattle might be able to find some explosive runs on the duo concepts that have troubled San Francisco. But would Seattle call enough of them? Gap concepts, jet sweeps and creative use of speedy playmakers like Rashid Shaheed (lined up as a running back for change-of-pace plays) could be the X-factor.

In the passing game, QB Sam Darnold will need to be aggressive, Tice said. The 49ers are vulnerable to chunk plays if you challenge the middle of the field. But Darnold is a high-variance player — sometimes brash enough to make those throws, sometimes a little trigger-happy and error-prone.

Both Tice and Harmon leaned toward the Seahawks pulling this one out, with Harmon predicting Seattle to cover the 3-point spread. "A little more sound sometimes," Tice said of Seattle, noting their discipline and ability to avoid breakdowns. Both hosts agreed: Seattle's defense was at worst the second-best in the league, and the Niners' offense hadn't yet faced a test like this.

But, just as crucially, the Seahawks' offense, though full of questions at running back and right guard, still "do the things you want to do — explosive passes" and, sometimes, that's what it takes to win.

articles.title: Jerry Jones put football aside during the Cowboys’ Week 4 game to help a player be there for a life-changing moment
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys linebacker Shemar James had more on his mind than football during the team’s Week 4 game against the Houston Texans.
articles.body: Dallas Cowboys linebacker Shemar James had more on his mind than football during the team’s Week 4 game against the Houston Texans. His wife, Erica Lewis, had gone into labor, and James learned the news at halftime. He stayed on the field and finished the game, but getting home quickly became his priority. The Cowboys won 34-30, yet the result was only part of the story. Owner Jerry Jones offered James a seat on the Jones family’s private plane, helping him reach his wife in time for the birth of their first child.Jerry Jones helped Shemar James get home after the Cowboys’ winJames was facing a race against time after learning that his wife was in labor. Lewis had gone into labor before kickoff but waited until halftime to tell him because she wanted him to remain focused on the game.The 22-year-old linebacker finished the contest before making arrangements to get back to Dallas. Jones then offered him a place on the family’s private plane, cutting down the journey home. An Uber was also waiting at the hangar to help James reach the hospital without losing more time.Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer shared the news with reporters after the game, making clear that James was already on his way home while others were still leaving the field."Shemar James' wife is in labor and he'll be flying home with the Joneses, and that's pretty cool," Schottenheimer said. "Praying for an easy delivery, and God is good."The assistance gave James a chance to be present for a moment that no professional football result could replace. He reached the hospital in time to witness the birth of his son, Shemar James Jr., who weighed 6 pounds, 10 ounces.Shemar James says the Jones family’s support meant a lotJames spoke about the experience with the Fort Worth Star-Telegram on Tuesday, October 6. He said the help showed that the organization cared about players beyond their work on the field."It was cool to see that they care more about just football," James told the publication. "They care about our personal lives. That meant a lot to me that the Jones family was able to allow me to get on the plane and have the Uber there waiting at the hangar to make it to my wife."James also described his reaction when he first heard the news at halftime. He knew he needed to get home as soon as the game ended, and he credited the Cowboys' support staff, including director of security Cable Johnson, for helping make the trip possible."My wife went into labor before the game, and she didn't want to tell me until halftime," he said. "She wanted to keep me focused on the game. It was kind of surreal. When I heard it, I was like, I got to go right now, but [Cowboys Director of Security] Cable Johnson and the support staff were so helpful."The birth ended a stressful day on a happy note. James said both his wife and son were healthy, and he was grateful to begin life as a father and husband. articles.title: 39% Mumbadevi voters out of draft roll, alleges Congress MLA Amin Patel
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Nearly 40% of Mumbadevi assembly constituency’s voters have been categorised as permanently shifted, dead, untraceable/absent, duplicate and
articles.body: MUMBAI: Nearly 40% of Mumbadevi assembly constituency’s voters have been categorised as permanently shifted, dead, untraceable/absent, duplicate and ‘other reasons’ during SIR, local Congress MLA Amin Patel has alleged.Patel said that several voters had been wrongly placed in these categories and wrote to Maharashtra chief electoral officer S Chockalingam, urging him to ensure that no voter was marked in any of the five categories or otherwise excluded due to errors in data entry, processing or verification. He also questioned how information collected during SIR could be excluded from the draft roll and listed several voters “wrongly left out”. “Forms have been accepted from people, yet they have been marked as dead. There are so many such cases. In some places, people have been unable to find BLOs. Even where available, BLOs have no clarity on Form 6’s format following what SC said,” Patel said.Patel has represented Mumbadevi, a mixed-population constituency that includes Dongri, Nagpada and Kamathipura, since 2009. The seat is considered a Congress stronghold.In his letter, Patel said BLOs had visited voters and collected the prescribed forms and details, making it difficult to understand how some of the same voters were subsequently excluded from the draft roll. He urged election authorities not to remove voters without proper verification.Chockalingam said he had not seen Patel’s letter and maintained that such categorisation was not specific to Mumbai or Maharashtra, citing urban mobility as a major factor.“Urban mobility is common across the country, where around 40% of people are not found at their original place during address and related verification process. We put them under five different categories and their names are not there on the draft list. They have the option of filing Form 6 to get themselves included in the list,” he said.Form 6 has recently been at the centre of controversy after a CJI-led SC bench rejected the Election Commission’s claim that the court had upheld the declaration attached to the form, making it clear that it had not approved any modification to it.State electoral officials said they would accept Form 6 applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure and in view of the SC’s observations. Decisions on the applications will be taken in accordance with the final outcome of the court proceedings.In Maharashtra, the enumeration exercise has been completed and electoral officials have verified voter details. Officials said BLOs collected information and signatures from residents, while voters reported dead, shifted elsewhere, absent from their registered addresses or found to have duplicate entries in another area were excluded from the draft roll.Electoral officials said public representatives had also been asked to verify the published draft roll and flag missing or incorrect names.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Los Buccaneers estrenan su casillero de victorias frente a los Cowboys
articles.standfirst: Jalon Daniels lideró a los Buccaneers con 189 yardas
articles.summary: Jalon Daniels lideró a los Buccaneers con 189 yardas
articles.body: Los Tampa Bay Buccaneers lograron la primera victoria de la temporada tras imponerse este jueves 16-24 a los Dallas Cowboys en el partido que abrió la semana cinco de la NFL. Jalon Daniels lideró a los Buccaneers con 189 yardas y un 19/25 en pases, incluido un 'touchdown', en la que fue la segunda titularidad de su carrera. Además, Bucky Irving fue un azote constante para la defensa texana, con 165 yardas en 21 carreras, y sumó un 'touchdown'. Enfrente, Dak Prescott pasó para 316 yardas con un 24/42 de acierto y un 'touchdown' para los Cowboys, aunque sumó dos intercepciones. El equipo texano fue el primero en golpear gracias a una carrera de Javonte Williams que subió el 7-0 en el marcador tras la primera posesión del partido. Sin embargo, los Buccaneers igualaron el encuentro en la siguiente posesión, que se alargó más de diez minutos, y en la que Daniels firmó un 8/8 en lanzamientos. A este inicio de fuegos artificiales le siguió la calma en el segundo cuarto, en el que solo una patada de tres puntos de Brandon Aubrey para los texanos a falta de 21 segundos movió el marcador para reflejar el 10-7. Gracias a la motivación -o quizás a la presión- por lograr la primera victoria de la temporada, los Buccaneers tiñeron completamente de rojo el tercer cuarto impulsados por un fantástico Irving. El 'running back' abrió el tercer cuarto con una carrera de 72 yardas, que Emeka Egbuka transformó en el 10-14 en la siguiente jugada. Inmediatamente después, Yaya Diaby firmó la primera intercepción de su carrera en su yarda 25, e Irving castigó de nuevo el error con un 'touchdown' de carrera (10-21), precedido por una ganancia previa de 64 yardas de Daniels que retrató a la endeble secundaria de Dallas. Cuando el guion parecía imposible de empeorar para los Cowboys, los Buccaneers forzaron un 'fumble' y recuperaron la posesión en el 'kickoff', entre la incredulidad de la parroquia texana. Cerraron el tercer cuarto con una patada de tres puntos para el 10-24. Los 'Bucs' pudieron sellar el partido a 8 minutos del final, pero una extraña decisión, en la que erraron un cuarto 'down' a una yarda de la zona de anotación, cuando podían sellar el partido con una patada, dio alas a los Cowboys. Los locales rozaron la remontada gracias a un 'touchdown' de George Pickens que puso el 16-24, pero fallaron la conversión de 2 puntos. Aunque llegaron a la 25 rival a falta de dos minutos, un pase de Prescott que golpeó en el casco del receptor y salió rebotado hacia el cielo, fue interceptado y sentenció el partido. Los Buccaneers son último de la NFC Sur con 1 victoria y 4 derrotas, mientras que los Cowboys caen a la tercera plaza de la NFC Este con un balance de 2 triunfos y 3 encuentros perdidos

articles.title: Matt Goncalves carries his late father's dream every time he takes the field
articles.summary: Colts guard Matt Goncalves, who spent his first two seasons dealing with new work, is becoming one of the NFL’s best offensive linemen
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Matt Goncalves has always understood the power of belief.

His father, William, always believed deeply in his son's ability to play professionally.

From the time he was little until his father passed away following a battle with cancer last October, Goncalves could lean on his father's confidence, a belief that helped carry him from Eastport-South Manor High to Pittsburgh to the Colts , all the way to a starting job in his second season in the NFL.

"He made me love the game, he made me believe in myself," Goncalves said. "An important thing is, it helped me believe in myself as much as my dad did. He believed in me more than everybody."

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

The talent was there. When the Colts drafted Goncalves in the third round of the 2024 draft, they thought they were taking a future right tackle.

Goncalves made nine starts at tackle as a rookie, building confidence in his ability to play at the NFL level, then got shifted to fill a hole on the interior of the offensive line. He'd been a tackle for most of his life; playing guard required Goncalves to essentially spend his first season as a starter in rookie mode, learning on the fly while starting for the Colts.

But that first season as a starting guard clarified what he needed to do in the offseason.

"The strength aspect of it," Goncalves said. "Working different body positions, being in a three-point stance, how to fire out off of that. Striking quickly, because they're on top of you before you know it. Understanding that, maybe a different scheme, it definitely brings a different perspective into what you want to incorporate in your training."

Goncalves also realized he needed to get his mind in a different place.

He had spent his first two seasons learning, and there's an inherent uncertainty that comes with trying to pick up something on the fly.

"This is the NFL," Goncalves said. "It's hard. It's a lot of stress, it's a lot of anxiety. You have expectations to perform, it's kind of hard to get to that state to kind of believe in yourself and be confident. You're worrying about this, that and the other thing. When you kind of just block those things out, focus on your job, have fun, believe in yourself and know the play, it'll take care of itself."

Goncalves needed to develop the kind of belief that his father always had in him.

"I made a lot of changes in my attitude and my mindset," Goncalves said. "Just go have fun. Believe in myself; I think belief is a powerful thing."

When he returned to the Colts this offseason, Goncalves was a different kind of player.

Even if he didn't realize it at first. A reporter asked Goncalves in training camp if he felt like a veteran, and at the time, he wasn't sure how to answer. Goncalves isn't the type of player to sing his own praises.

Four games into the season, Goncalves can see a difference now.

He knows the position, knows how he's supposed to approach positional drills to fix his technique or take it to the next level. When he gets into the building every morning, Goncalves knows everybody he's passing in the hallways, knows the routine he has to use to get ready for Sunday.

"That gives me confidence," Goncalves said. "'I've got this, I'm a vet.'"

The rest of the Colts offensive line can tell a difference.

"He's poised, he's a pro," left tackle Bernhard Raimann said. "He takes care of all the little details. You can see how much he prepares every week, how much winning matters to him."

The Indianapolis offense is off to a rough start, and young Colts right tackle Jalen Travis is going through growing pains.

But the right guard has been a rock for Indianapolis, stabilizing the right side of the line next to Travis. Goncalves has not given up a "blown block" in the passing game, according to Sports Info Solutions, and he's been almost perfect in the run game as well, a rarity for a lineman after four games.

"His technique, the way he finishes blocks, his physicality in the run game, his poise in pass pro, his hands, it's been great," Raimann said. "It's been phenomenal."

Goncalves has also become the kind of lineman that young players like Jalen Farmer can watch and try to emulate.

"Works really hard at it," Colts quarterback Daniel Jones said. "No surprise, he's playing at a high level."

Every time Goncalves puts his hand in the dirt, he thinks of his dad, who died almost a year ago.

When he plays on Pittsburgh's field again this weekend, those thoughts will likely be even stronger, given his history in college.

"This is our dream together, to get to this level," Goncalves said. "I have two other brothers. Obviously, they played basketball, baseball. His dream was to see his sons go play for a professional sports team."

He's gotten to the point his father always believed he'd reach.

articles.title: Grading Every New NFL Head Coach Entering Week 5 of the 2026 Season
articles.summary: Consider the first term complete.
articles.body:
We're about a quarter of the way through the 2026 NFL season. While it's too early to draw conclusions about the league's 10 new head coaches, we can at least grade them based on how well each has started.

Here's a breakdown from Brady to Stefanski—with the understanding that win-loss records rarely tell the whole story.

Demonstrated Strengths: Brady's offense is the league's highest-scoring unit and has led the NFL in explosive plays for four weeks. Ultimately, that's his primary responsibility.

Needs Improvement: The Bills actually laid eggs in both Week 3 and Week 4. The Chargers let them off the hook in the first case, but their luck ran out against New England. This team could very easily be 1-3 instead of 3-1.

Demonstrated Strengths: Hafley's defense has been somewhat of a pleasant surprise. That unit gave up zero touchdowns against the Vikings in Week 4 and allowed an average of 19.5 points per game over the last two weeks against the formidable Chiefs and Vikings. On top of that, one of the league's least talented teams has shown plenty of fight.

Needs Improvement: The team has developed a reputation for starting slowly. Hafley needs to work on his overall game and clock management. That should come with time.

Demonstrated Strengths: Harbaugh has provided an immediate culture reset, stabilizing the franchise. Despite several supposedly back-breaking injuries, he's got a rebuilding team in first place and tied for the NFC lead with eight takeaways.

Needs Improvement: They actually came extremely close to losing to the bad Cardinals and worse Titans. Let's see how they fare when the schedule toughens up in November and December.

Demonstrated Strengths: Kubiak has the rebuilding Raiders competing hard every week. His offense ranks eighth in scoring. The league's third-least-penalized team has taken a significant step forward after winning just seven games over the last two seasons.

Needs Improvement: That offensive unit has committed six turnovers. Kubiak could afford to be more creative and a little less stubborn with the run game.

Demonstrated Strengths: The Cardinals are one of 12 teams that have scored at least 24 points in three of their first four games. They got an impressive win out of the gate and have been competitive more often than not despite a lack of overall talent.

Needs Improvement: That offense has generated only five 20-plus-yard plays all season, easily the worst mark in the NFL (only one other team has fewer than 10). LaFleur also did not manage the second half well in a tough Week 4 loss to the Giants.

Demonstrated Strengths: Despite the slow overall start, McCarthy's offense does rank in the top 10 in the league with 17 plays of 20-plus yards. The Steelers are the league's fifth-least-penalized team through four weeks.

Needs Improvement: The offense has scored touchdowns on just four of nine red-zone trips. Only three units in the NFL have been worse at converting third downs. That explains why they rank in the bottom 10 in scoring overall. The playmaking defense is the main reason they're 2-2 against a so-so schedule.

Demonstrated Strengths: Just one hiccup thus far, as the Ravens are in first place. The offense was humming before potentially losing Lamar Jackson. The defense might be turning a corner.

Needs Improvement: His defense, which is giving up 24 points per game, has surrendered a subpar 15 gains of 20-plus yards in four weeks and ranks in the bottom 10 in pressure rate. Meanwhile, only Cleveland and Green Bay have been penalized more.

Demonstrated Strengths: Deshaun Watson has yet to bomb, and the offense has been fairly productive despite having to acclimate following an offseason of substantial change. The team appears to be buying in, as the culture shift is palpable.

Needs Improvement: That offense has scored touchdowns on just five of 10 red-zone trips. They rank in the bottom 10 at converting third downs. The Browns also enter Week 5 as the NFL's most penalized team, so it's a work in progress.

Demonstrated Strengths: Saleh's defense has surrendered the ninth-fewest points in the league. The Titans have also shown discipline, as one of only four teams penalized fewer than 25 times so far. They didn't look prepared at all out of the gate but have since been competitive in three consecutive outings.

Needs Improvement: That D has generated just two takeaways in four games, both of which came in Week 2. The offense also remains anemic.

Demonstrated Strengths: His offense has scored touchdowns on eight of 10 red-zone trips, becoming a top-10 unit overall. They have been lighting it up after a slow start. A lot of that is because Stefanski has seemingly unlocked Michael Penix Jr.

Needs Improvement: Only three offenses have committed more turnovers than Atlanta's (eight), although five of those came from backup quarterbacks in a Week 2 nightmare performance against Carolina.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns Biggest Team Needs and Trade Targets
articles.summary: Sitting at 3-1 after the first four games of the season, the Cleveland Browns are in a better position than most expected at this point.
articles.body:
Sitting at 3-1 after the first four games of the season, the Cleveland Browns are in a better position than most expected at this point.

Todd Monken seems to have things heading in the right direction. The Browns are far from perfect. They still have a negative point differential. They're still one of the most penalized teams in football. They rank 26th in ESPN's FPI rankings.

Yet, they're sitting atop the AFC North and have a very manageable schedule over the next several weeks.

There's even a case to be made that the Browns could be buyers as the NFL trade deadline approaches in November.

Here's a look at the roster spots that could use reinforcements and the potential trade targets they should watch for if they find themselves in the playoff race.

Tytus Howard, Dawand Jones, KT Leveston (Practice Squad), Eze Obinna (Practice Squad)

Tytus Howard was supposed to be brought in as a high-floor veteran to stabilize the offensive line. Through four games, that has simply not been the case.

Howard has been a consistent culprit behind the Browns' offensive operational issues. He has five false starts and has yet to go a game without jumping offsides at least once.

The 30-year-old's pass protection has been an issue as well. He's given up two sacks and has seven blown blocks, per Sports Info Solutions . It's going to be time to give Dawand Jones a shot or bring in another player if Howard doesn't step up his game.

Here's the reality check for the right tackle situation. A starting quality tackle trade is a rarity. Few teams are willing to part with competent players at the position at this time of year.

Austin Jackson could be an exception. The former first-round pick is on a one-year contract and struggling in Jeff Hafley's first year as the Dolphins' head coach. The Fins could be ready to dump him after a 0-4 start to the season.

A change of scenery could be mutually beneficial.

Walker Little has guard-tackle versatility and proven experience. Yet, he has become a reserve in Jacksonville. The Jags might not be willing to part with depth on the line, but it would be worth it for Andrew Berry to check in with James Gladstone.

Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell, Myles Harden, Noah Igbinoghene, Toriano Pride Jr., Mekhi Blackmon, Michael Coats Jr. (Practice Squad), Myles Bryant (Practice Squad)

The Browns are playing a ton of man coverage, and Denzel Ward is doing it at a high level. The rest of the corners have been suspect. Tyson Campbell is giving up a passer rating of 116.7 when targeted. Myles Harden has been inconsistent in the slot.

What's even more concerning is that Campbell has already dealt with injuries this season. The Browns' cornerback depth is going to be tested. It's scary to think about how the secondary looks without Ward, who has never played a full season.

Kristian Fulton, Brandon Stephens, Amik Robertson

Getting a team to part with a corner capable of playing press-man is a tricky task, but there are a few fits that would make sense. Kristian Fulton has found himself as the odd man out in Kansas City. He has only allowed three receptions on seven targets, but he's also played just 58 percent of the snaps in three games.

Monken knows Brandon Stephens from their time together in Baltimore, but Stephens is off to a hot start with the Jets so far this season. New York is sitting at 1-3 through the first four weeks and could be willing to deal.

Amik Robertson can't play press-man on the outside, but he's the kind of physical veteran slot who could push Harden. The Commanders are also 1-3, so they could be looking to offload veterans at the deadline.

Quinshon Judkins, Raheim Sanders, Jaleel McLaughlin, Dylan Sampson (IR)

Judkins has been one of the most disappointing players on the roster this year. The offensive line isn't perfect, but Judkins has just a 40.7 success rate this season. He's averaging 3.0 yards per carry.

Sanders has made some good plays, especially as a receiver out of the backfield. Jaleel McLaughlin was signed and scored a touchdown on Thursday Night Football against the Steelers, but the Browns need a running back to actually boost the ground game.

Tony Pollard, Tyler Allgeier, Kenneth Gainwell

The first two targets here are the most intriguing. Sanders and even McLaughlin have proven they can be secondary backs who help in the passing game. Targeting Kenneth Gainwell would just be a more experienced version of that kind of back.

What the Browns really could use is another back to share the between-the-tackles and early-down runs Judkins currently gets. Pollard is the lead back in Tennessee, but he's 29 and in the final year of his contract. They have Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singleton to take over.

Tyler Allgeier has successfully shared backfield duties in Arizona and Atlanta. However, Jeremiyah Love is going to continue to push for a bigger piece of the pie for the Cardinals right now.

Mason Graham (injured), Maliek Collins, Mike Hall Jr., Adin Huntington, Sam Kamara (Practice Squad), Zion Logue (Practice Squad), Chris Williams (Practice Squad), Elijah Chatman (IR)

The Browns were fortunate that Mason Graham avoided a season-ending injury after his hot start to the season. He leads the way with four sacks, but Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN classified his MCL and ankle sprain as a "multi-week absence."

The Browns' interior without Graham is a bit scary, and not in a good way. Maliek Collins is a solid veteran, but Adin Huntington is undersized and Michael Hall Jr. is dealing with an ankle injury .

A'Shawn Robinson, Solomon Thomas, Davon Godchaux

Ideally, the Browns would be able to swing a deal for a low-cost veteran. Run-stopping is probably more important than pass-rushing in the long term. Graham will eventually be back.

Robinson is a run-stuffing specialist. The Buccaneers are at the point where they may need to deal for veterans at the deadline. Solomon Thomas is a bit more of a tweener, but he has a ton of experience in even fronts and would offer a steady veteran presence.

Godchaux would offer size (6'4", 330) that the Browns don't really have on the interior right now. At 1-3, the Saints might be shifting to younger options in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills' Biggest Team Needs and Trade Targets
articles.summary: Technically, the Buffalo Bills are halfway to the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Technically, the Buffalo Bills are halfway to the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

The Bills, four games into their season, will play their eighth game on Nov. 9, less than 24 hours before the deadline hits at 4 p.m. ET the following day.

At this point, several positional needs have become accentuated by on-field performances and/or injuries, causing fans to start thinking about who might be available between now and Nov. 10.

With that in mind, here's an updated breakdown of the team's key needs and potential trade targets at each position over the coming weeks.

On the Roster: Christian Benford, Maxwell Hairston, Dee Alford, Davison Igbinosun

Benford struggled mightily before suffering a toe injury in Week 3. Hairston was bullied in coverage as the top cover guy in Week 4. Alford has lacked consistency and is now dealing with an ankle injury. Igbinosun is a rookie the team would prefer not to rely on heavily this early.

Kelee Ringo, Philadelphia Eagles: A natural perimeter cover man, Ringo remains buried on Philadelphia's depth chart in the midst of a walk year. With the Eagles likely open to dealing him out of conference, he should come at a low cost and could potentially challenge Benford or Hairston for reps in a new environment.

Rasul Douglas, Washington Commanders: Could history repeat itself? Brandon Beane acquired Douglas at the 2023 deadline. It would make sense to inquire about him again if the Commanders' season continues to go downhill. The 31-year-old is on a cheap one-year deal in Washington, where he has an interception and has given up just 11 completions on 20 passes into his coverage. This would be an interesting rental scenario.

Carrington Valentine, Green Bay Packers: The Packers could easily lose their next three games to Chicago, Dallas and Detroit to become clear sellers. If so, trading Valentine would make sense, as he works through the final year of his rookie contract while stuck behind Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. The Bills would be getting a cheap, motivated 25-year-old with fairly significant starting experience on the perimeter.

Don't forget about Tre'Davious White, who started 16 games for the Bills last season and remains an unrestricted free agent. I'm not sure what he has left at 31, but I'd trust him as much as any corner the team has right now.

On the Roster: Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, Kaleb Elarms-Orr, Joe Andreessen

Bernard and Williams are not playmakers. Both go missing for long stretches, as neither is a consistent producer. There's just no oomph here. Elarms-Orr is merely a fourth-round rookie. Andreessen is a dependable special-teams contributor, but that's his ceiling.

Ivan Pace Jr., Minnesota Vikings: A disruptive pass rusher inside the tackles when he plays consistently, Pace has fallen out of favor in Brian Flores' defense. As a result, he'd likely be affordable with an expiring contract and could be rejuvenated in a new setting.

Mack Wilson, Arizona Cardinals: The Cardinals are clearly far from a competitive window. Wilson is an eight-year veteran wrapping up a three-year contract. He's unlikely to be part of this rebuild when he turns 29 this offseason, but he'd bring plenty of physicality to Buffalo while improving the defense's ability to cover tight ends.

Patrick Queen, Pittsburgh Steelers: This one's highly unlikely, but Queen is in a contract year and the Steelers aren't looking overly competitive. If Pittsburgh goes off the rails between now and early November, the Steelers could become major sellers and take what they can get for the 27-year-old two-time Pro Bowler.

Matt Milano and Shaq Thompson played a combined 1,165 snaps in this defense last season, as both remain viable options—Milano as a street free agent and Thompson as an in-house elevation from the practice squad. Thompson is on the practice squad. It's obviously a new look now. Both are 32, but they could still provide a boost if everything aligns.

On the Roster: DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Joshua Palmer, Skyler Bell, Greg Dortch

Moore has been awesome when present but has been plagued by a nagging shoulder injury since Week 2. Coleman and Shakir are great secondary options but are up and down. Palmer doesn't look like anything more than a No. 4 target. Bell is a fourth-round rookie who hasn't been active on game day, while Dortch is pretty much strictly a returner.

Tank Dell, Houston Texans: I'm thinking of a scenario where Dell finally returns to health soon but finds himself out of favor in a receiving corps that also features Nico Collins, Jaylin Noel and Kayshon Boutte. He's in a walk year, as the Texans are winless. This could be a worthwhile flier.

Chris Godwin, Tampa Bay Buccaneers: The Bucs are 0-4 as the 30-year-old Godwin is effectively in a walk year. Tampa Bay can walk away from his contract with minimal dead money this offseason. He might be running out of gas but is still on pace to catch 68 passes in an otherwise unproductive offense this season. If the Bills continue to run into injury issues in the receiving corps, this would be a nice veteran pickup who would help a lot as a blocker as well.

Stefon Diggs, Washington Commanders: This is a reunion a lot of Bills fans would feel uncomfortable with, but if the team becomes desperate between now and the deadline, it isn't out of the question. Back before Diggs signed with Washington in the offseason, Joe Brady didn't rule out the possibility of the 32-year-old returning to Western New York. For what it's worth, Diggs did score three touchdowns in the first two weeks for a Commanders team that does not look like a contender.

At the very least, the team could soon consider activating Bell in place of Palmer if the top three guys are healthy. Eventually, they gotta see what they have there.

On the more extreme side, Drew Rosenhaus recently suggested that fading superstar Tyreek Hill could soon sign with a new team—although that type of potential culture shakeup probably wouldn't be worth it unless things truly go off the rails.

A middle ground might be another attempt to resurrect Gabe Davis, who peaked about four years ago in Buffalo but is still only 27.

That said, it's not time to panic yet about the Buffalo receiving corps.

articles.title: The Super Bowl hopefuls making major changes only a month into the season
articles.summary: The head coaches of the Denver Broncos and the Houston Texans are taking over play-calling duties after subpar starts to their seasons.
articles.body: The Denver Broncos and the Houston Texans entered the 2026 NFL season as Super Bowl hopefuls, particularly after having suffered bitter defeats in the later rounds of the most recent playoffs. Both teams, however, have struggled through the first four weeks of this year. And now both hope making the same change will ignite their teams: The head coaches are taking back control of play-calling duties. For the Broncos, head coach Sean Payton — one of the most respected offensive minds in the game — made the curious decision to hand play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Davis Webb this year. Payton has been asked about the switch after nearly every game this season, and on Thursday, he announced he would now be the one to call plays amid reports of a change. “Everyone is disappointed in the unit itself,” Payton said of the offense while deflecting blame from Webb. “We’re 2-2, but we feel like there’s more there.” He added of the change: “It’s about buttoning up all the little things that keep you from sustaining drives.” Denver’s offense has been one of the least effective in the NFL this season. The Broncos ranked 27th in points and yards per game entering Week 5. The advanced stats aren’t much better, as Denver ranks 20th in expected points added (EPA) per play, per Sumer Sports. The Broncos haven’t been able to push the ball downfield. They rank 27th in explosive play rate and 25th in yards per play, according to Sharp Football Analysis. The passing attack’s average depth of target is only 6.01 yards, second lowest in the NFL. “I want to be aggressive,” quarterback Bo Nix told reporters Wednesday, but he added that he’s trying to find the right balance between aggression and making smart decisions. “When it’s open, let’s hit it. But at the same time, I’ve been gotten too many times trying to do too much. In this day and age in our offense, I don’t have to be a hero on every play. I don’t have to do too much. ... If you’re not careful, turnovers may go through the roof, and that’s just not what I need to be doing.” Meanwhile, in Houston, the Texans are even more desperate after an 0-4 start. Only one team in NFL history has made the playoffs after having dropped its first four games. Houston has been close to this position before, having reached the postseason after an 0-3 start last year. The issue for the Texans has been their defense, as head coach DeMeco Ryans will take the reins from defensive coordinator Matt Burke when it comes to calling plays. “It’s a tough decision to make,” Ryans told reporters Wednesday. “It’s also, as a head coach, I have a lot of tough decisions I have to make, and it’s always my decisions, and sometimes they’re not always a popular opinion. I’m not in this role to please a lot of people’s opinions. I have to do what’s best for this team and make sure I’m leading in that way.” Said defensive end Will Anderson: “I think what DeMeco brings [is] that style of coaching where he’s going to call you out. He’s going to make sure that you know exactly what you’re going to do, what you need to do and what you didn’t do.” Houston’s defensive drop has been shocking, as the team was expected to have one of the best units in the league. Last season, the Texans ranked no lower than sixth in points, total yards and pass yards allowed per game. This year, Houston enters Week 5 at 26th in points allowed, 20th in total yards allowed and 28th in pass yards allowed. After quarterback C.J. Stroud struggled in last winter’s playoff run, there was a belief the Texans could be dominant if Stroud merely had an average season. Instead, he has been solid, and it hasn’t mattered. Houston is 15th in EPA per dropback so far this season, as Stroud has thrown for five touchdowns and no interceptions. In three of the team’s first four games, he led go-ahead drives in the fourth quarter. But the defense has given up game-winning drives in each of those games. Entering Week 4, the Texans are 26th in EPA per play on defense. If there were ever an ideal time for Payton and Ryans to take back control of play calling, it’s before Week 5 in particular. Both the Broncos and the Texans will be playing winless teams Sunday, as Denver plays the 0-4 Los Angeles Chargers, while Houston draws the 0-4 Tennessee Titans. If neither the Broncos nor the Texans can bounce back against two of the worst teams in the league, then whoever is calling the plays could end up being the least of their problems.
