articles.title: Trevor Lawrence for MVP? George Kittle's San Francisco 49ers for the Super Bowl? Bijan Robinson to run riot? - NFL Gameday Guide
articles.summary: Watch the Jacksonville Jaguars face the Philadelphia Eagles in the second NFL London game of the season at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, live on Sky Sports from 2pm, followed by the Green Bay Packers against the Chicago Bears and the San Francisco 49ers against the Seattle Seahawks
articles.body:
It will see Jags punter Logan Cooke play in an NFL-record 10th international game to surpass former Jacksonville offensive lineman Tyler Shatley, per ESPN stats.

But this has a different feel to that of the Jags teams from years gone by, who have monopolised London without ever truly inserting themselves among football's Super Bowl contenders. The 2017 team that stunned the NFL to reach the AFC Championship Game, perhaps, being the exception to that rule.

This time they arrive to take on the Philadelphia Eagles behind a true MVP candidate in Trevor Lawrence and a head coach in Liam Coen knocking on the door of the elite. It is not a team brimming with star names, but instead an expertly-drilled reflection of their coach's vision for contention.

The Jags are 3-1 and purring at the top of the AFC South, their one blemish a defeat to the Denver Broncos in which they can been control before letting the game slip away.

Momentum is on their side after back-to-back statement wins over the New England Patriots and Cincinnati Bengals, in contrast to an opponent battling to steady a ship rocked by injury, retirement and consecutive losses. There is an overwhelming case of deja vu for the Eagles, whose soaring expectations can occasionally make for a gloomier fan outlook than is actually the case.

The last time the Eagles faced the Jaguars, Saquon Barkley conjured one of the greatest plays in NFL history with his reverse hurdle over Jacksonville cornerback Jarrian Jones back in November 2024.

"Everybody DM'd me like I'm supposed to be mad or something," Jones said on Wednesday. "I don't give a damn. He made a good play. It is what it is."

Barkley's availability for Sunday is in doubt after the running back exited Week Four's defeat to the Los Angeles Rams with a hamstring injury. The Eagles had already been missing leading wide receiver DeVonta Smith due to a hamstring issue, the former Heisman Trophy winner having become Jalen Hurts' unequivocal top target this offseason following the marquee departure of AJ Brown.

This week meanwhile saw stalwart offensive tackle Lane Johnson announce his shock retirement to focus on his mental health, before center Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. What's more, wide receiver Hollywood Brown, edge rusher Jonathan Greenard and linebacker Jihaad Campbell all missed practice this week through injury.

On paper, it is a decimated Eagles team so far failing to demonstrate the kind of offensive resurgence expected under Sean Mannion after he replaced Kevin Patullo as offensive coordinator in the offseason. Philly's offense enters Sunday's game at Tottenham averaging the fourth-fewest yards per game, second-fewest passing yards per game, 26th in scoring and 29th in EPA/play.

Jalen Hurts also continues to be one of the most divisive quarterbacks in football as critics wrestle over his true value, who is suffering in a system lacking serious punch on the ground and the consistent presence of a Brown on the outside - with the greatest of respect to the always-reliable hands of Smith.

The Jags have their identity. The Eagles are still searching desperately for theirs.

Nick Sirianni's side have elected to fly in just 36 hours before kickoff in London, following a similar plan to that of Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams when they travelled in on the eve of their dominant win over the Jaguars at Wembley.

Philadelphia Eagles @ Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - KO 2.30pm - LIVE from 2pm on Sky Sports NFL and Sky Sports+:

The Jags might have finally found their answer as to how best they use Travis Hunter. Both he and they started this partnership with the best intentions of revolutionising football with a full-time two-way player, Hunter having famously starred at receiver and corner in college. To drift from as much wouldn't be to concede defeat, but instead recognise Hunter's potential to become one of the premier defensive backs in football. Right now, that looks like where his future lies. Hunter played 71 defensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Bengals and gave up just four catches for 30 yards while seeing an interception nullified by a penalty up front. Receiver packages can still be in play from time to time, but the signs are there of Hunter finally making his mark in the NFL, on defense.

Chicago Bears @ Green Bay Packers - KO 6pm - Exclusively LIVE from 6pm on Sky Sports NFL, Sky Sports Football and part on Sky Sports Main Event:

Ben Johnson's Chicago Bears offense enters Sunday's rivalry matchup boasting the No 1-ranked rushing attack in football behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, who lead a ground unit averaging 196.3 yards per game. It has become the perfect remedy to the loss of starting quarterback Caleb Williams, teeing up Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent for success in his absence. Bagent will start again on Sunday as Chicago arrive 3-1 against a Packers side yet to convince after a 2-2 start. Matt LaFleur's offense ranks dead last in offense amid the absence of Josh Jacobs due to his off-field legal problems, while they are also averaging a fifth-fewest points per game.

Minnesota Vikings @ New Orleans Saints - KO 6pm - LIVE from 6pm on Sky Sports+:

Tyler Shough is braced for one of the defining acid tests of his young NFL career as the New Orleans Saints quarterback comes up against a Brian Flores defense that has spearheaded the Minnesota Vikings to a 4-0 start this season. The Vikings are ranked third in pressures with 72, according to Pro Football Focus, while leading the league in points allowed. Dallas Turner is ranked second with 5.5 sacks behind only Buffalo's Greg Rousseau amid what is shaping up as a breakout season, thriving in a defense that leads the NFL by a distance with a blitz rate of almost 70 per cent.

San Francisco 49ers @ Seattle Seahawks - KO 9.25pm - Exclusively LIVE from 9.15pm on Sky Sports NFL, Sky Sports Football, and part on Sky Sports Main Event:

If the San Francisco 49ers are to be serious Super Bowl contenders, they need this version of George Kittle for an entire undisrupted season. The way he moved on Sunday's 56-yard touchdown catch-and-run, you would not believe he is just coming off a season-ending torn Achilles. It was Kittle at his electric best, executing a perfect blitz-crushing Kyle Shanahan call to underline everything that makes this 49ers offense so innovative and so dangerous when everybody is healthy. Kittle has 16 catches for 244 yards and four touchdowns so far in 2026 as part of a 49ers attack ranked seventh in yards and third in scoring.

Detroit Lions @ Arizona Cardinals - KO 9.25pm - Exclusively LIVE from 9.25pm on Sky Sports Football:

The Cardinals are coming off last weekend's 36-24 defeat to the Giants, during which Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions while both start running back Jeremiyah Love and tight end Trey McBride were largely bottled up as the focal points of their offense. Sunday welcomes two of the NFL's most porous defenses, the Lions allowing a second-most 31.8 points per game to the Cardinals' fourth-most 29.3. Jared Goff has been clean even if not spectacular over the first month of the campaign, 109 of 161 passing for a second-most 1,214 yards and nine touchdowns to zero interceptions. He is the only quarterback ever in NFL history to have 1,200-plus passing yards with zero turnovers through four games of a season while not having a winning record, according to Opta Stats. The Lions come into Sunday 2-2 after losing 32-26 to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday night.

Baltimore Ravens @ Atlanta Falcons - KO 1.20am (Monday) - LIVE from 1.10am (Monday) on Sky Sports NFL and Sky Sports Main Event:

The Atlanta Falcons look a completely different proposition to the team that began the season 0-2 behind backup quarterback Cooper Rush. Michael Penix Jr has flourished on his return from injury in victories over the Packers and Saints, completing 73.3 per cent of his passes for 479 yards and two touchdowns. With some stability at quarterback has come deserved reward for Bijan Robinson, who is second only to Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III with 614 yards from scrimmage through the first month. That includes 339 yards and four touchdowns on the ground over the last two weeks alone. Lamar Jackson availability is meanwhile in question after the ankle injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans in Week Four, with Tyler Huntley in line to start should the two-time MVP miss out. Declan Doyle is still perhaps in second gear with his Ravens offense, which itself looks a completely different threat with Zay Flowers in the lineup as a field-flipping aerial complement to Jackson and Derrick Henry on the ground. The Ravens are averaging the fifth-most yards and fifth-most rushing yards per game after a 3-1 start.

The Commanders are set to have quarterback Jayden Daniels available again against the Giants this weekend after he missed the last two weeks with an elbow injury

Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans is taking over defensive play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Matt Burke after the team's 0-4 start

Eagles offensive tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement from the NFL in what is his 14th season in the league

The Seahawks opted against signing running back Joe Mixon after the veteran's physical with the team

Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's job is 'not in jeopardy' after the team's 0-4 start

The Vikings signed veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr to their practice squad

Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is one more game with a rushing touchdown and a touchdown pass from becoming the fifth quarterback with 30 such games in NFL history behind Josh Allen, Cam Newton, Aaron Rodgers and Steve Young.

Jags quarterback Trevor Lawrence needs one more touchdown pass in London to tie Blake Bortles' nine for the second-most touchdown passes in regular-season international games; Tom Brady leads the way with 12.

49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is one of two quarterbacks with to post a passer rating of 125 or higher in multiple games this season.

Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs needs one more touchdown to tie Barry Sanders (57) for the most scrimmage touchdowns by a player under the age of 25 in NFL history.

Saints running back Alvin Kamara needs just five receiving yards against the Vikings to become the sixth player in NFL history with at least 5,000 rushing yards and 5,000 receiving yards.

articles.title: Cowboys' Dak Prescott Addresses Viral Video of Person Yelling 'Embarrassing' After Loss to Bucs
articles.summary: The criticisms of the Dallas Cowboys are now coming from inside the house following their 24-16 loss on Thursday night to the previously-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
The criticisms of the Dallas Cowboys are now coming from inside the house following their 24-16 loss on Thursday night to the previously-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

As Dak Prescott was talking back to the locker room at AT&T Stadium, someone in the tunnel area was heard yelling "embarrassing."

Prescott told reporters after the game the person "looked away" when he turned back to see who it was:

"When he said it, I just happened to look at him, and at that point, he looked away. And when I turned my head back, he said something else. And so that's the part that, just as a man or as just a person, feel free to speak your mind — just speak it. Don't cower away from the reaction that you're going to get. And so, if you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing. If you're saying it to me, then say it to me. Don't go back on it. So that's all that was, and hate that it's even being talked about, to be honest with you."

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the situation was "motivating" for the team because "we believe in what we're doing" and they will work to get back on track.

According to ESPN's Todd Archer , the person who made the comment was a third-party contractor who was standing outside of the players' exit from the stadium field.

Prescott did not want to use the term "embarrassing" to describe this performance, but he explained it was a game that was set up for the Cowboys to win.

Entering Thursday night, Dallas appeared in good position to snag a victory and move over the .500 mark for the first time all season. The Bucs entered the day with an 0-4 record, had to travel to AT&T Stadium on a short week and were starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback.

Instead, the Cowboys defense once again couldn't get stops. Christian Parker's unit gave up 419 total yards, including 241 on the ground. It was the third-most rushing yards by a team in a game this season.

The Bucs did not commit a turnover for the first time all season. They had nine turnovers in the first four weeks, third-most in the NFL.

Dallas' offense wasn't effective in part because it was one-dimensional. The Cowboys had 50 rushing yards on 13 attempts. Prescott was picked off twice, though both turnovers bounced off the hands of his intended receivers.

Coming off a dramatic win over the Houston Texans on Sunday, the Cowboys seemed poised to go on a run with a favorable schedule that included the Bucs, Green Bay Packers, Philadelphia Eagles and Arizona Cardinals.

Instead, the Cowboys dropped to 2-3 with many of the same issues that plagued them last season. Joey Porter Jr., who didn't play due to illness, will help solve some of those problems when he does take the field.

But an outside cornerback isn't likely to help a leaky run defense that was supposed to be improved after adding Quinnen Williams, Rashan Gary, Von Miller and Malachi Lawrence to their front four in the past 12 months.

articles.title: Predicting NFL's Next Coaching Moves After Sean Payton, DeMeco Ryans Take Back Play-Calling Duties
articles.summary: Several teams have fallen short of expectations through the first month of the season, which has led to the first significant in-season changes of 2026. No head coaches have been fired yet, but a couple of significant moves were made ahead of Week 5.
articles.body:
Several teams have fallen short of expectations through the first month of the season, which has led to the first significant in-season changes of 2026. No head coaches have been fired yet, but a couple of significant moves were made ahead of Week 5.

Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans announced on Wednesday that he is taking over the defensive play-calling duties previously held by coordinator Matt Burke. A day later, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton is expected to replace offensive coordinator Davis Webb as his team's primary play-caller.

The 0-4 Texans and 2-2- Broncos aren't the only teams that have underperformed through four full weeks, and they certainly won't be the last teams to shake things up on the sideline.

Here, find predictions for the next coaching dominoes to drop based on recent performances, projected results, available options, and any relevant recent buzz.

Lions Replace Defensive Coordinator Kelvin Sheppard

Kelvin Sheppard took over as the Detroit Lions' defensive coordinator before the 2025 season, and his unit's performance has underwhelmed since. Last year's defense finished the season ranked 18th overall and 22nd in points allowed. This year, the group has been even worse.

The Lions rank 31st in points allowed and dead-last in yards allowed through Week 4. They've also lost two games in convincing fashion on the road because of ineffective defense.

To this point, head coach Dan Campbell hasn't entertained the idea of replacing Sheppard.

"I'm not talking about all that," Campbell said, per ESPN's Eric Woodyard . "I'm talking about getting better right now with what we've got."

However, Detroit cannot continue to give up 30-plus points almost every week and expect to make a run in the NFC North. If the defense again collapses against the Arizona Cardinals this week, the Lions might even consider making changes at the Week 6 bye—ahead of pivotal matchups against the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings.

Defensive line coach and run-game coordinator Kacy Rodgers would be a logical candidate to replace Sheppard on an interim basis, as he has defensive-coordinator experience on his resume.

Chargers Replace Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel

Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is another play-caller who has received some in-season support from his head coach.

"No, his job is not in jeopardy," head coach Jim Harbaugh said of McDaniel, per Shane Lantz of the Associated Press. "He's a skilled coach and we're going to keep growing."

The problem, though, isn't simply that Los Angeles' offense has underwhelmed, though it has. The Chargers remain winless largely because they rank 21st in yards and 29th in scoring. However, the bigger issue is that quarterback Justin Herbert seems to have regressed in McDaniel's system.

Herbert has thrown just four touchdowns with six interceptions. He also holds a 70.6 passer rating, by far the worst of his career and nearly 25 points below his career average.

The Chargers' season isn't quite lost, but losses to the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs over the next two weeks could leave L.A. eyeing the future and considering changes during the Week 7 bye. Herbert is under contract through 2029, and Harbaugh needs to get him back on a positive track.

Passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach Shane Day has experience with Herbert that dates back to his rookie season—though he spent the 2023 season in Houston—and he could be the perfect candidate to help the quarterback return to form.

Day's play-calling experiences is limited to a brief window in college, but he has a strong grasp of what has traditionally worked for Herbert and the Chargers.

Saints Replace Defensive Coordinator Brandon Staley as Play-Caller

The New Orleans Saints looked like a potential contender at the beginning of the year. They took the Detroit Lions to overtime in Week 1, and they pulled off a road upset over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2.

However, the Saints have lost back-to-back games, and they appeared woefully outclassed by the rival Atlanta Falcons on Monday night. With tough games against the Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants, and Pittsburgh Steelers upcoming, New Orleans' promising start to the season might appear fraudulent by the Week 8 bye.

If the Saints were to make a change during their bye week, it would likely involve defensive coordinator Brandon Staley. His unit has been hampered by injuries, but it has been one of the league's worst units even when healthy. New Orleans ranks 26th in total defense and 32nd in points allowed.

The Saints defense has consistently exhibited poor gap integrity, bad tackling, and frequent coverage breakdowns in the secondary. A fresh voice might help resolve some of these issues.

New Orleans might not outright fire Staley, but it might consider handing play-calling duties over to defensive pass game coordinator Terry Joseph.

Joseph is relatively new to the NFL ranks, having joined New Orleans in 2025, and he doesn't have a coordinator background. However, he's a respected coach who was listed as a breakout coaching candidate during the summer by The Athletic's Jourdan Rodrigue . His experience coaching and developing the secondary could also be critical as the Saints look to tighten their back end.

Cowboys Find Help for Defensive Coordinator Christian Parker

The Dallas Cowboys put a lot of effort into rebuilding their defense this offseason, adding the likes of Rashan Gary, Von Miller, Caleb Downs , and Malachi Lawrence . Last week, they traded for cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

However, Dallas' defense has performed an awful lot like last year's unit. The Cowboys came into Week 5 ranked 30th in yards allowed and 28th in points allowed. On Thursday night, they surrendered 419 yards and 24 points in a loss to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers and undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels.

New defensive coordinator Christian Parker is rightfully under scrutiny, and longtime NFL coordinator Don Martindale has publicly offered his assistance.

"He's being outclassed right now," Martindale told Talkin' Ball with Pat Leonard (h/t ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio ). "So Jerry [Jones] can call me and I'll go help him. But, you know, I'm talking about helping the coordinator."

The Cowboys might not call Martindale specifically, but no one should be surprised if they look to give Parker a helping hand. However, they could look to add a veteran coach in an advisory role or consider giving more play-calling input to another defensive coach.

Passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach Derrick Ansley would be a strong candidate for the latter route, as he has coordinator experience—though he didn't call defensive plays until after the Chargers fired head coach Brandon Staley in 2023.

Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles could be the first head coach to lose his job in 2026, depending on the team's ability to build on Thursday's win. That victory certainly helps, and Bowles has a bit of a built-in excuse for the 1-4 start as quarterback Baker Mayfield is sidelined by a dislocated thumb.

However, Tampa's offense was an overall disaster in the first month under new coordinator Zac Robinson, who was hired by Bowles, and that's only been part of the issue. Bowles, who was elevated from the defensive-coordinator role in 2022 when Bruce Arians transitioned to a front-office role, hasn't gotten great production out of the other side of the ball either.

The Buccaneers entered Week 5 ranked fourth in total defense but only 19th in points allowed. Some of the unit's letdowns have been the result of Bowles' decision-making. His clock and situational management have long been questionable, and Bowles hasn't delivered consecutive wins since last October.

Bowles inherited a Super Bowl-caliber team, and while he kept it competitive for a few years in the post-Tom Brady era, Tampa may be well past its peak under Bowles guidance.

The Bucs have a talented core, and they would undoubtedly provide a coveted job if they have a head-coaching vacancy in 2027. Firing Bowles in-season—possibly even before the Week 9 bye—could give Tampa a head start on its coaching search.

Run-game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote would be an intriguing candidate to replace Bowles on an interim basis. His experience working with both sides of the ball, along with his experience as a player, would give him a unique voice with which to guide the team.

Foote played in the NFL for 13 seasons, and he won a pair of Super Bowls with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The New York Jets hired former Lions offensive coordinator Aaron Glenn as their head coach at the start of the 2025 season. He went 3-14 in his inaugural campaign but managed to survive through the offseason.

The Jets fired offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand and defensive coordinator Steve Wilks while making several other coaching changes following last season.

Glenn's second season got off to a promising start with a Week 1 victory and an overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers. Of course, the win came against the now-0-4 Tennessee Titans, while the Packers haven't looked very formidable during their 2-2 start.

Perhaps more importantly, New York might be sitting at 2-2 itself had Glenn done a better job of managing the game against Green Bay.

The Jets did keep things relatively close against the Lions and Chicago Bears over the last two weeks, and they may not be inclined to move away from Glenn before the Week 12 bye. However, it's fair to wonder if he's the right coach to lead New York beyond this season.

New York has three 2027 first-round picks and is widely expected to chase its quarterback of the future in April's draft. Pairing said quarterback with a new head coach might be the move for the Jets.

If Glenn is relieved of his duties, offensive coordinator Frank Reich is the most likely interim candidate. He has had two head-coaching stints in the NFL, and he could continue developing young offensive players like offensive tackle Olu Fashanu, receiver Adonai Mitchell, and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq .

articles.title: Worker tells Cowboys QB Dak Prescott loss to winless Buccaneers was 'embarrassing'
articles.summary: The loss drops the Cowboys to 2-3 on the season.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys fans inside AT&T Stadium let the players hear it throughout their 24-16 defeat on Thursday night to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The lack of execution throughout, including on a two-point conversation try late in the fourth quarter with the Cowboys trailing by eight, led to boos as Dallas fell to 2-3 on the season and suffered its second straight loss at home.

It wasn't just the fans inside the stadium letting the players know how they felt. As the players walked back to the locker room after the game, a contract-car service driver, who was standing outside of the players' exit at the stadium, said "embarrassing" as quarterback Dak Prescott walked by.

"When he said it, I just happened to look at him, and at that point, he looked away," said Prescott, who noted the person wasn't "wrong" in his assessment. "And when I turned my head back, he said something else. And so that's the part that, just as a man or as just a person, feel free to speak your mind — just speak it. Don't cower away from the reaction that you're going to get.

"If you're saying it's embarrassing, say it's embarrassing. If you're saying it to me, then say it to me. Don't go back on it. So that's all that was, and hate it that it's even being talked about, to be honest with you."

The Buccaneers' win marked only the sixth time in Cowboys history that they lost to a team with a 0-4 record or worse.

Prescott added that Thursday night was one of those games on a team's schedule that they were "supposed to have on paper."

"I think [head coach Brian Schottenheimer] said it best in the locker room: In this league, you've got to win the games you're supposed to win," Prescott said. "And when a winless team comes into your home stadium in a Thursday night primetime game, yeah, we're supposed to win that."

The 16 points are the lowest scored by the Cowboys since Week 3 of last season. They recorded just 50 rushing yards, their lowest since Week 16 in 2024, and allowed at least 20 points for the 12th straight game dating back to last season.

Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving ran for 165 yards , including a 72-yarder early in the third quarter, and undrafted quarterback Jalon Daniels threw for a career-high 189 yards in his second NFL start.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said eyes are on the defense, but first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker is in no danger of having his play-calling duties reassigned, something Jones said was "premature."

"Certainly, he's sitting there with taking it on the shoulders, which goes with the territory, but I feel that he's competent," Jones said.

The Cowboys will remain on primetime in their next two games with Week 6's Sunday night matchup against the Green Bay Packers before taking on the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night in Week 7.

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb Injury Update, New Rumors on Return Timeline After Exiting Cowboys' Loss vs. Bucs
articles.summary: Despite a bad 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night, the Dallas Cowboys may have good news about CeeDee Lamb's injury coming out of the game.
articles.body:
Despite a bad 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night, the Dallas Cowboys may have good news about CeeDee Lamb's injury coming out of the game.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Lamb suffered a quad bruise that is "not expected to be a long-term" issue.

Lamb originally injured his leg during the Cowboys' win over the Houston Texans on Sunday. He was officially listed on the injury report leading up to Thursday's game with a thigh injury, though he was a full practice participant throughout the week.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters after losing to the Bucs that Lamb took a hit to the same thigh.

Lamb was at one point seen walking to the locker room in the fourth quarter.

According to ESPN's Todd Archer , Lamb's quad tightened up after he was hit in the area by a Buccaneers defender.

Lamb played a season-low 34 offensive snaps against Tampa Bay. It was his first time playing fewer than 70 percent of the Cowboys' total offensive snaps in a game since Week 18 last season.

The Bucs held Lamb to just nine yards on two receptions. He put up more than 100 yards in the previous three games, including 189 yards on 17 receptions against the Texans.

Lamb does benefit from playing early this week, giving him extra time off going into Week 6. The Cowboys will play the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football on Oct. 18.

articles.title: Week 5 Waiver Wire Pickups, Best Fantasy Sleepers to Target After Box Score Review
articles.summary: Week 5 got off to an unexpected start on Thursday, as the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers earned a 24-16 victory over the Cowboys in Dallas.
articles.body:
Week 5 got off to an unexpected start on Thursday, as the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers earned a 24-16 victory over the Cowboys in Dallas.

While The Week 5 opener may have taken many fans by surprise, no one was shocked to see the Dallas defense struggle, even against undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. The Cowboys have been a favorable matchup for opposing offenses, and represent exactly the sort of matchup fantasy managers should be targeting for the rest of Week 5.

Daniels, by the way, threw for 189 yards and a touchdown while adding 23 yards on the ground.

Here, we'll examine some Week 5 sleepers who may still be available on the waiver wire and who are worth considering based on recent production and projected matchups.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

The Arizona Cardinals are sitting at 1-3, but they have a strong offensive cast, headlined by Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jeremiyah Love. This has helped make Jacoby Brissett a viable streamer in fantasy.

Brissett has thrown multiple touchdowns in each of his last two games, and he has a tremendous matchup against the Detroit Lions this week.

The Lions' defense has been arguably the worst in the league this season and has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks than any other squad. Last Sunday night, Detroit allowed Bryce Young to go off for 329 yards and two touchdowns.

Brissett has legitimate top-10 scoring potential this week. He's still only rostered in 33 percent of fantasy leagues.

To be clear, the Jacksonville Jaguars aren't a friendly matchup for opposing running backs. The Jags' defense has surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to the position, and it could be aided by location in Week 5.

Jacksonville will host the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and London Games are often lacking in offense.

However, Will Shipley could be worth a flex start based on workload alone. Saquon Barkley is considered week-to-week with a hamstring injury and is unlikely to play this week, according to Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer.

With Tank Bigsby now on injured reserve, Will Shipley should see opportunities early and often. He was a popular add off of waivers this week but is still only rostered in 44 percent of fantasy leagues.

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson is a late-week must-add in most scoring formats. The third-year pass-catcher has become one of Aaron Rodgers' preferred targets, and he's on a significantly upward trajectory.

Wilson has seen six targets in every game this season, and in each of his last two, he has produced at least three catches, 60 yards, and one touchdown.

This week, Wilson could see an even bigger role as Michael Pittman Jr. is expected to miss multiple weeks with a foot injury. He'll have a reasonable matchup against an Indianapolis Colts defense that has surrendered the 13th-most fantasy points to opposing receivers this season.

There's a very good chance that Wilson is available, too, as he is rostered in just one percent of fantasy leagues.

Cincinnati Bengals tight end is another virtual must-add, and he has an even more enticing matchup than Wilson does. The Miami Dolphins have surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

Gesicki really operates as more of a big slot receiver in Cincinnati's offense, and he could see extra targets this week because of injuries. Ja'Marr Chase has returned to practice but suffered a concussion last week. Tee Higgins is dealing with an adductor injury and has been out of practice this week.

At times, Gesicki has shown that he can be a focal point of the offense. He had five grabs for 78 yards and a touchdown in Week 1, and he had three catches for 40 yards and a score last week. If the Bengals are thin at receiver in Miami, Joe Burrow will likely turn to Gesicki frequently.

Gesicki is still only rostered in 26 percent of fantasy leagues.

articles.title: Jason Kelce: Ex-Philadelphia Eagles star plays amateur rugby game in London
articles.summary: Former Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl winner Jason Kelce stuns amateur London rugby players by showing up for a practice game.
articles.body:
Amateur rugby union players from Hackney had a shock when they turned up for a training match - to see a former Super Bowl champion among the opposition.

Hackney RFC's players rocked up on Wednesday for a 30-minute friendly, only to find former NFL star Jason Kelce playing for local rivals Old Streetonians.

Kelce - older brother of Travis, the three-time Super Bowl winning Kansas City Chiefs tight end married to global pop superstar Taylor Swift - played 13 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles.

The 38-year-old is now learning to play different sports for his YouTube channel, and had a rugby lesson from former Harlequins and England prop Joe Marler.

"It's a nice little story being able to say we played rugby against Taylor Swift's brother-in-law, which I'm sure he loves as a title," Hackney full-back Peter Scott joked to BBC Sport.

"It's amazing that the sporting community, not even just the rugby community, can make these sorts of things happen. It was pretty surreal and it's pretty cool."

Kelce was part of Philadelphia's 2018 Super Bowl winning side and earned seven selections to the Pro Bowl - the annual NFL game featuring the league's top players - before retiring in 2024.

He was joined by former Philadelphia team-mate Beau Allen, also a member of that Eagles championship side of eight years ago, at Hackney Marshes in London this week.

Eagles stun Patriots in Super Bowl LII Published 5 February 2018

Get American Football news sent straight to your phone

'I put him on his back - then he ran through me'

Hackney prop Dave Lewis told BBC Sport it took Kelce - a former center, an offensive lineman, whose main role is to snap the ball to the quarterback and then protect him, each play - a while to get used to rugby's rules.

"We got a message from our club captain saying our local rivals were coming down with two ex-NFL players, but we didn't know anything else about it," Lewis said.

"With the rules, he got there. At the very start, he sort of went round the back of a ruck and picked the ball up, which he obviously was then penalised for.

"I handed him off at one point and put him on his back in front of his team-mates and all of our fans as well. I hope they release that footage because I'll be dining out on it forever if they do.

"He just got back up and absolutely smashed me later on when he had the ball, running through me. So, I don't think he has an ego. I think he's just up for the physicality of it all."

Lewis' team-mate Scott said he thought Kelce picked the game up pretty quickly.

"He's a pretty intimidating figure," Scott added. "Very broad shoulders, powerful legs. They were using him as a number 8, which, I think, is the perfect position for him.

"There were a few intricacies, like how he was carrying the ball and where he was in the scrum, but he clearly knew what he was. He didn't look out of place at all.

"In rugby you are taught to tackle at an angle, and go at people's shoulders. He was a lot more front on, like 'OK, route one, I'm just gonna go straight at anyone that came out'."

Kelce is in England this week to commentate on Sunday's NFL overseas game between his former club Philadelphia and the Jacksonville Jaguars at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium (14:30 BST).

Old Street chairman Will Gilgrass said both Kelce and Allen really embraced the whole opportunity.

"They were very good value in the pub afterwards," he said. "We took them to one of our locals, and they put their cards behind the bar, chatting with the lads for a few hours after the game and really getting involved.

"They even did our initiation, singing a song and downing a pint."

The Hackney players also had their 15 minutes of fame after the match, with Kelce's American film crew interviewing some of them.

"They were asking how he got on, and what were the major differences to translate to an NFL audience," said Scott.

"The one I picked up on was the amount of power that he was able to generate after he would get tackled. His leg drives were sensational. It felt like three people would hit him and then he would go for another 20 metres.

"American football seems to be all about short, sharp, explosive power and he had that in spades - like he was rapid, very powerful, and then would take a backseat for a little while and then come back and do it again."

articles.title: Beyond $375M FOX Sports broadcasting deal - how is Tom Brady building his sports empire
articles.summary: NFL legend Tom Brady signed a 10-year, $375 million broadcasting contract with FOX Sports in 2022. It keeps him locked through the 2032 season.
articles.body: NFL legend Tom Brady signed a 10-year, $375 million broadcasting contract with FOX Sports in 2022. It keeps him locked through the 2032 season. The network’s lead NFL game analyst earns an annual salary of $37.5 million. His $37.5 million yearly income makes him the highest-paid sports broadcaster in history.He plays the role of lead NFL color commentator alongside play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt, plus promotional ambassador duties. He began broadcasting in the 2024 NFL season following his retirement from the league.Tom Brady expands his sports franchise ownership portfolioThe seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady has quietly built his post-NFL career that extends far beyond the broadcasting booth. He has conveniently and strategically moved into sports ownership, advisory roles, and emerging leagues. This gives him an omnipotent presence across several professional sports franchises.Rather than stepping away from competition after retiring following the 2022 NFL season, Brady positioned himself closer than ever to the decision-making sphere of sports.His ever-growing sports franchise portfolio comprises the NFL’s Las Vegas Raiders, the WNBA’s Las Vegas Aces, English soccer club Birmingham City, and Team Brady in the UIM E1 World Championship. He has also been a crucial part of the ownership group behind Major League Pickleball’s Las Vegas Night Owls.Tom Brady’s Las Vegas Raiders ownership and football operations roleTom Brady’s most massive ownership move came in the NFL, the very league where he played and won seven Super Bowl championships. League owners unanimously approved Brady’s purchase of a 5% stake in the Las Vegas Raiders in October 2024.His partner, Tom Wagner, co-founder and co-CEO of Knighthead Capital Management, holds an additional interest in the team.The league-ownership approval was met with conflicting discussions about Brady’s simultaneous role as FOX Sports’ lead NFL analyst and how there could be a potential conflict of interest between broadcasting and team ownership.NFL insider Adam Schefter reported in Sept. 2025 that the league announced that Tom Brady, who is a minority owner with the Las Vegas Raiders and also a broadcaster for FOX Sports, is “prohibited from going to a team facility for practices or production meetings.” But the NFL legend is allowed to sit in the coaches’ booth.Brady’s involvement expanded beyond merely owning a financial share. Las Vegas Raiders Mark Davis announced in January 2026 that general manager John Spytek would lead football operations in close collaboration with Tom Brady.This gave the NFL legend a valid opportunity to offer his valuable perspective without suggesting that he runs the franchise and also has a broadcasting role, where he reportedly cannot take any team’s side.The father of three also described his role in a more modest way. He said that he was a limited partner and a sounding board rather than someone who micromanaged the franchise.However, Las Vegas Raiders QB Kirk Cousins revealed in April 2026 that Brady was just a phone call away from him - speaking of the seven-time Super Bowl champion’s involvement in the team he’s purchased despite being a broadcasting booth personnel.“Tom’s been great. I texted him, called him, and he actually FaceTimed me while I was at a baseball practice,” Cousins said.Cousins added, “He just wants to be a resource. I don’t know that he’s going to be around all the time. But he’s always a phone call, text away. And I think, to have a guy who’s won seven Super Bowls, a phone call or a text away, who’s embedded in your organization, it’s got to be a positive.”Tom Brady’s WNBA ownership and Birmingham City soccer investment strategyAs for other sports franchises, Tom Brady is not limited to the NFL. In 2023, a year before he part-owned the Las Vegas Raiders, he acquired an ownership interest in the Las Vegas Aces of the WNBA, where he joined Mark Davis.A year’s worth of working with Mark Davis could have built a stable foundation for him to infiltrate the Las Vegas Raiders of the NFL.Anyhow, Brady has spoken about his admiration for women’s sports and the opportunity to contribute to the WNBA’s continued growth. “I’m very excited to be a part of the Las Vegas Aces organization,” Brady said.“My love for women’s sports began at a young age when I would tag along to all my older sisters’ games. They were by far the best athletes in our house. We celebrated their accomplishments together as a family, and they remain a great inspiration to me.I have always been a huge fan of women’s sports. And I admire the work that the Aces’ players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes. To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor.”That same year, Brady became a minority investor in Birmingham City. articles.body: En agosto de 2015, John Urschel, jugador entonces de los Baltimore Ravens, sufrió una conmoción cerebral grave, pero continuó jugando. Sin embargo, dos años después, el canadiense optó por abandonar el fútbol americano tras conocer las consecuencias de la encefalopatía traumática crónica (ETC), una enfermedad cerebral degenerativa que afecta a muchos exjugadores de ésta y otras disciplinas, debido a los golpes durante los encuentros. Urschel decidió entonces centrarse en sus estudios de matemáticas en el prestigioso Instituto Tecnológico de Massachusetts (MIT), los que había empezado cuando jugaba en la NFL. Ahora, con un doctorado, imparte clases sobre la materia en las mismas aulas en las que estudió. Pero su nombre trascendió en el mundo académico tras publicar hace unos días un artículo titulado 'Sobre el factor de crecimiento de matrices aleatorias', en el que el canadiense explica cómo ha encontrado la solución a un problema matemático que permanecía sin resolver desde la década de 1990, cuando llegaron los algoritmos. Ese algoritmo, conocido como eliminación gaussiana, había generado soluciones con éxito en millones de aplicaciones prácticas, pero para los matemáticos eso no es suficiente, ya que ellos deben determinar si los métodos o conceptos funcionan en todos los casos posibles. Urschel demostró matemáticamente las condiciones exactas que garantizan esa fiabilidad. “Resulta muy interesante que el algoritmo más importante que tenemos en este campo no lo entendamos del todo”, dijo Urschel al 'Washington Post'. “Me encanta esta pregunta del por qué frente al cómo, y esta idea de comprender qué está sucediendo”.

Ditka is one of the most successful players who made the transition into coaching in NFL history. He had a 12-year playing career from 1961 to 1972 with the Bears, Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles.

During his first season, Ditka set an NFL rookie tight end record with 1,076 receiving yards. The mark stood until 2024 when Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders surpassed it.

Ditka's 12 touchdown catches in 1961 remain the most for a rookie tight end. He won an NFL championship with the Bears in 1963 and Super Bowl VI with the Cowboys during the 1971 season.

After retiring as a player in March 1973, Ditka immediately went into coaching as an assistant with the Cowboys on Tom Landry's staff. He remained in Dallas for nine seasons before the Bears hired him as their head coach in 1982.

The Bears went 11-14 in Ditka's first two seasons before hitting their stride in 1984. They had a run of five consecutive seasons with double-digit wins, highlighted by the iconic 1985 team that went 15-1 en route to the only Super Bowl victory in franchise history.

Ditka spent 11 seasons as head coach in Chicago. He spent four years away from the sidelines before returning for a three-year stint as head coach of the New Orleans Saints from 1997 to 1999.

articles.title: Mike Ditka, legendary Chicago Bears coach, dies at 86
articles.summary: Legendary Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka, who led the team to its only Super Bowl victory in 1986, has died, his family announced.
articles.body: Legendary Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka, who led the team to its only Super Bowl victory in 1986, has died, his family announced. He was 86. “It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka,” the family said in a statement Friday. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family,” the statement said. “Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.” The Bears released a statement saying Ditka’s impact on the team as “a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable.” Ditka, the statement said, “created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations.” Ditka, who was inducted into the pro football Hall of Fame in 1988, was remembered by the organization’s president Jim Porter as a player who “brought an unrivaled level of toughness to an era already defined by physicality.” “He brought that same philosophy to his coaching,” Porter said in a statement. Tough and pugnacious, Ditka personified the hard-hitting team he led to a 46-10 thrashing of the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX and was called “Iron Mike,” both because of his gruff demeanor and because he hailed from a steel town in western Pennsylvania. Ditka, who was born Michael Dyczko on Oct. 18, 1939, became a beloved figure in the Windy City and the embodiment of Chicago’s blue-collar, tough-guy identity. In the years after the Bears won the Super Bowl, Ditka was immortalized by “Saturday Night Live” in the “Bill Swerski’s Superfans” sketches, which featured a group of fans singing his praises to the point of absurdity with tick Chicawgo ayccents. “If I may shift gears for a moment gentlemen, coach Ditka vs. The Hurricane, who would win?” the Bill Swerski character says in one skit. “Ditka! Ditka!,” the others reply. The oldest of four children, Ditka was the son of a welder of Polish and Ukrainian stock who changed his name to make it easier to pronounce. But growing up in the town of Aliquippa, Ditka excelled at the all-American sport of football and that earned him a scholarship and a ticket out of town to the University of Pittsburgh, where he initially planned to study dentistry. Instead, Ditka excelled on the gridiron and in 1961 he was drafted by the Bears as a tight end. There, Ditka redefined a position that mostly consisted of blocking for rushers by becoming a scoring machine who racked up a dozen touchdowns in his first season and was named Rookie of the Year. Ditka was a star on the 1963 Bears championship, in the pre-Super Bowl era, and a pro-bowler in each of the five seasons he played for “Da Bears.” He also gained some infamy by decking a fan who ran out on the field in the middle of a championship game broadcast on national TV. “Ditka has been trained since high school to knock down anything that moves,” famous Chicago newspaper columnist Mike Royko wrote in Sept. 1966. “The young man flew into the air. He was limp when he landed and shaky when the police led him away.” Unable to reach a contract agreement with Bears owner and coach George Halas, Ditka signed with the Houston Oilers in 1987 for the then-princely sum of $300,000. Halas, Ditka said disparagingly, “threw nickels around like manhole covers.” Ditka went on to play for the Dallas Cowboys, where in 1972 he caught a touchdown pass in their 24–3 victory over the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI. After retiring in 1973, Ditka was hired by the Cowboys as an assistant coach. And during his nine seasons there, Dallas made the playoffs eight times, won six division titles, three NFC championships, and a Super Bowl victory in 1977. “Ditka was the first man enshrined in Canton who had won Super Bowls as a player, assistant coach and head coach,” the Hall of Fame said in a statement.

articles.title: Mike Ditka, the quintessential Chicago Bear, dies at 86
articles.summary: Mike Ditka, who won NFL titles as a player and coach with the Chicago Bears, has died. He was 86.
articles.body: Mike Ditka, who won NFL titles as a player and coach with the Chicago Bears, has died. He was 86. Ditka’s family announced the death on Friday in a statement. “It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka,” the family said. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.” Nicknamed “Iron Mike” as a player, Ditka helped revolutionize the tight-end position, then moved to the sidelines and took over as Chicago’s coach. His 1985 team featured one of the game’s most dominant defenses ever. It also had enough outsized personalities to record a rap video, “The Super Bowl Shuffle,” and back up their boasting in the championship game three months later. After retiring as a coach, Ditka became a restaurateur, pitchman and TV personality, as well as a forceful advocate for improved medical and retirement benefits for former players. Ditka was tough and gruff, the quintessential Chicago Bear. He did everything from order off the menu to knock defensive backs on their butts with a growl. His adopted hometown reveled in every minute. Still revered as “Da Coach” and ringmaster of the 1985 Bears, one of the most dominant and perhaps the zaniest Super Bowl-winning team in league history. Ditka was enshrined in the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame and the Bears said during a ceremony in 2013 that his “No. 89” jersey will be the last one retired by the team. He was born in Carnegie, Pennsylvania, the son of a welder who changed the family name from Dyczko. He grew up in nearby Aliquippa, close to the coal-mining and steel-manufacturing plants that dotted the western part of the state, a big, talented, three-sport athlete and All-American at Pitt whose bruising style made his first nickname, “Iron Mike,” a good fit. Selected fifth overall by flinty Chicago owner George Halas in the 1961 draft, Ditka went on to Rookie of the Year honors, multiple Pro Bowl trips and the 1963 NFL Championship. In the bargain, he and Baltimore’s John Mackey changed the tight end position and offensive schemes forever. He was a battering ram of a blocker, but Ditka was just as likely to catch a short pass and pinball through an entire secondary or outrace a lone safety on a deep touchdown throw. He left Chicago in 1966, playing briefly for Philadelphia and Dallas. He moved to the sideline in 1973 as an assistant to the revered Tom Landry and stayed with the Cowboys for eight seasons, before returning to a hero’s welcome in Chicago as head coach in 1982. Ditka’s return to the Bears lasted 10 tumultuous years, including five straight NFC Central titles, the Super Bowl win, a DUI conviction, a heart attack, a long-running feud with defensive coordinator Buddy Ryan and, finally, a new nickname – “Da Coach.” To Hall of Fame linebacker Mike Singletary, the seeds of what was to come were planted in Ditka’s first meeting with the team. He laid out his vision, saying Chicago would be in the Super Bowl in three years – and many of the players in the room would not be around for it. “When I first heard him when he walked in the room, to me Coach Ditka had the opportunity to be the greatest coach of all time because he had the fire,” Singletary said at the Bears’ 100th anniversary celebration in June 2019. “I don’t know George Halas coached. But I can imagine that the fire and intensity and passion that Coach Ditka exuded that first day set the tone for exactly what he said: ‘Three years from now, we’re going to be in the Super Bowl.’ And that was 1982. In ’85, we were there and it was because of that vision.” The public beefs with Ryan mirrored the behind-the-scenes battles that Ditka waged trying to contain a team bristling with outsized personalities. “It was more than a team,” Ditka once said. “It was a team of characters that had character that played for a crazy man, who let him be crazy and had fun doing it and don’t apologize for it ever. I wouldn’t want to be one of these suits walking around on the sideline today. “I have no desire to be that. I was what I was and they were what they were and, damn, it was fun.” It wasn’t until two dozen players recorded “The Super Bowl Shuffle” – an audacious rap-styled video released three months ahead of the 1986 title game – that the rest of the football world wondered whether Ditka was losing his grip. His players never did. “We call him ‘Sybil’ after that girl in the movie,” quarterback Jim McMahon once explained. “You know, the one that had all those personalities. Mike will be calm one minute, then throw a clipboard the next. People don’t understand that, but we do.” The Bears demolished the New England Patriots 46-10 in the Super Bowl, but Ditka often said he regretted having McMahon and defensive tackle William “The Refrigerator” Perry run for touchdowns instead of Walter Payton, Chicago’s loyal and long-suffering running back. Ryan departed for a head coaching job in Philadelphia soon after. While the Bears continued to be a contender for most of the next five years, a 5-11 season prompted Ditka’s departure in 1992. After a five-year absence, he returned to coaching with the New Orleans Saints, but failed to revive the franchise. After a miserable 1999 season ended with a 3-13 record – Ditka’s worst as either a player or coach – he left the sidelines for good. His face and demeanor were so familiar by then that a second act became an easy segue. Ditka began building a stable of restaurants and appeared as himself in TV sitcoms from “Cheers” to “Third Rock from the Sun,” as well as shows such as “L.A. Law” and “Saturday Night Live.” He also stayed close to the game as an NFL analyst and game-day show personality at ESPN. Ditka’s high-profile status also made him an effective advocate to secure improved health and retirement benefits for former players. His name also circulated for years in Illinois political circles. Though he never ran for office, Ditka described himself as a staunch conservative and was mentioned several times as a possible Republican candidate, including a congressional race against then state Rep. Barack Obama for the US Senate.

articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones discussed the team's continued defensive struggles during a 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and quarterback Jalon Daniels on Thursday night.

"Surprising isn't even a big enough word," Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. "It's mind boggling looking at the stats of our last five games."

He isn't looking to make any staff changes yet, though.

"(That) is just not in the best interest of our team," Jones said, per Machota . "We played five games. We have 12 more regular season games and hopefully playoff games to go."

The Cowboys allowed 419 yards to a Buccaneers offense led by Daniels, an undrafted rookie who opened the regular season as the team's backup quarterback.

He finished 19-of-25 for 189 yards and one touchdown without committing a turnover. Daniels also rushed for 23 yards.

It marked the second start of his career.

Tampa Bay was able to control the clock throughout the contest, as it had the ball for over 39 minutes of game time. Meanwhile, Dallas had possession for just under 21 minutes.

The Buccaneers consistently moved the chains during the game, averaging 6.4 yards per play while converting seven of their 13 opportunities on third down.

For the Cowboys, the loss represented another disappointing performance for a defense that was looking to take a step forward after allowing a league-worst 30.1 points per game during their 2025 campaign.

Dallas added pass-rusher Rashan Gary in an offseason trade with the Green Bay Packers before bolstering its secondary by signing safety Jalen Thompson and cornerback Cobie Durant in free agency.

The Cowboys picked safety Caleb Downs with the No. 11 overall selection in the 2026 NFL draft as well.

While it's worth noting that players such as Thompson and Durant have missed time due to injuries, Dallas' defense hasn't been able to meet expectations through five games.

The Cowboys are allowing 27.2 points and 395.4 total yards per game, with the latter ranking No. 31 among all teams.

With Thursday's defeat, Dallas fell to 2-3 to start the 2026 season.

articles.title: Mike Ditka, Chicago Bears Hall of Fame legend, dies at 86
articles.summary: Ditka was best known for leading the 1985 Chicago Bears to the only Super Bowl title in franchise history.
articles.body:
Of all the quotes attributed to Mike Ditka over the years, there's one in particular that stands out when it comes to the way he lived his life in football.

"Living in the past is for cowards," the football legend once said. "If you live in the past, you die in the past."

Like many other things Ditka said, it was brash and impulsive. It made no pretensions about being delicate or polite.

It was, however, an accurate depiction of the way Ditka kept progressing and evolving in over 60 years of being involved with the sport. He succeeded more than he failed, but he claimed that didn't matter much.

"Success isn't permanent and failure isn't fatal," went one of Ditka's other famous quotes.

Ditka died on Friday, his family announced. He was 86.

Jarrett Payton, Walter Payton's son, announced the news on Chicago's 104.3 The Score. Payton shared a statement from the Ditka family on X :

It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka. While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever. With love and gratitude, The Ditka Family

In a football career that spanned nearly five decades, Ditka earned induction into both the College Football and Pro Football Hall of Fames, won NFL championships as a player, an assistant and a head coach, the latter coming in the 1985 season, when he led the Chicago Bears to its first and still only Super Bowl title.

The 1985 championship launched Ditka into a new level of fame. He cashed checks for pitching a wide variety of products, was lovingly lampooned on a classic "Saturday Night Live" sketch and became the closest thing the Chicago sporting scene has ever had to a patron saint.

But while Chicago's triumph over New England in January 1986 remained the high point in Ditka's career, it was far from the only highlight.

Indeed, few men have experienced Ditka's level or breadth of success in the game. His coaching days were preceded by a Hall of Fame playing career with the Bears and Cowboys, then followed with successful ventures in both broadcasting and business. In his later years, Ditka started the "Gridiron Greats Assistance Fund," an organization designed to help struggling ex-players who hadn't been rewarded as handsomely by the game as he was.

Though he looked as if he was from one of Chicago's many Polish neighborhoods, Ditka was born "Michael Dyczko" on Oct. 18, 1939 in Carnegie, Pennsylvania. The son of a welder, he played high school football in Aliquippa and his stardom in steel country gave him the "Iron Mike" nickname that would stick for decades after he left the state.

After a successful collegiate career at Pitt, Ditka was drafted by the Bears with the fifth overall pick in the 1961 NFL Draft. He won that season's Rookie of the Year award and was a key part of Chicago's 1963 NFL championship team under George Halas, the last Bears team to win a title until Halas hired Ditka to return the team to glory in the '80s.

Ditka was traded to the Eagles in 1967, but eventually landed in Dallas, where he won Super Bowl titles with the Cowboys both as a player (VI) and an assistant coach (XII). He and Oakland Raiders coach Tom Flores remain the only men to win Super Bowls as a player, assistant and coach.

After nearly a decade spent as an assistant under Cowboys legend Tom Landry, Ditka sent a letter to Halas saying he was "ready" to return home and lead the Bears. Halas took him up on his offer for the 1982 season and within three seasons, Ditka took the Bears to the NFC title game.

Ditka's leadership style could best be described as volatile, and his relationships with players, fellow coaches and media were far from perfect. Even though the egos belonging to Ditka and defensive coordinator Buddy Ryan could barely co-exist in the same locker room, the 1985 Bears became one of the sport's greatest teams, going 15-1 and shutting out two teams in the NFC playoffs before shellacking the Patriots 46-10 in Super Bowl XX.

Ryan left to become the Eagles' head coach after the Super Bowl. Ditka and the drama-filled and often injured Bears never again reached the top, soon outclassed in the NFC by San Francisco, Washington and New York. In later years, members of the '85 team would come out and say Ditka should've won at least one more title with the talent he had, a charge with which the coach himself later agreed.

Ditka was fired following the 1992 season, capping an 11-year run that saw the Bears go 106-62. He surfaced in New Orleans in 1997 for a three-year stint that would have been largely forgettable were it not for his decision to trade away all of the Saints' picks in 1999 (plus a first-rounder in 2000) for the right to move up and take Heisman Trophy winner Ricky Williams. The pair posed as a just-married couple for the cover of ESPN: The Magazine, with Williams donning a wedding dress.

Ditka remained visible after coaching career

Following his departure from New Orleans, Ditka resumed a broadcasting career he'd started with NBC and took jobs with CBS, then ESPN. He cultivated his personality into a successful and pervasive brand, running popular restaurants in the Chicagoland area and putting his visage on everything from fine wine and Bloody Mary mix to salsa and giardiniera, a spicy Italian relish that is popular in the Chicagoland area.

A staunch Republican, Ditka considered running for Illinois' open Senate seat in 2004 but ultimately decided against it.

A Democrat named Barack Obama ended up winning the office, and Ditka, with no small amount of bitterness, would later remark that the course of American history would have been different had he decided to pursue the office.

articles.title: NFL Exec Questions 'Blind Faith' in Arch Manning amid Debate over 2027 Draft's QB1
articles.summary: Amid a solid but unspectacular start to the season for Texas, Arch Manning's previous standing as the consensus No. 1 quarterback prospect in the 2027 NFL draft class is being called into question.
articles.body:
Amid a solid but unspectacular start to the season for Texas, Arch Manning's previous standing as the consensus No. 1 quarterback prospect in the 2027 NFL draft class is being called into question.

Speaking to ESPN's Jordan Reid , one assistant general manager for an AFC team questioned the "blind faith" some have put in Manning as the top signal-caller in the upcoming draft if he leaves school.

"What's giving so many people this blind faith that there's just this monstrous ceiling with him?" the assistant GM said. "Maybe this current state is just who he really is as a prospect."

A scout for an AFC club told Reid that Manning does have "fascinating" moments within games that make him tantalizing for NFL teams:

"He'll always be graded on a different scale because of the name, but I think someone will fall in love with what he can be in a few years. I don't think he's the best in the class, but his flashes in games are fascinating and a preview of what could happen down the road."

B/R's 2027 NFL draft big board coming into the season had Manning ranked as the No. 2 quarterback behind Miami's Darian Mensah and sixth-best player overall.

In the most recent rankings update released on Sept. 22, B/R's NFL scouting department dropped Manning down to No. 17 overall. Mensah, Oregon's Dante Moore and Mississippi's Trinidad Chambliss were all ahead of him among quarterbacks.

The physical tools for Manning will be hard for NFL scouts to ignore. He has prototypical size with a listed height of 6'4" and weight of 222 pounds.

In a recent mock draft from Nate Tice of Yahoo Sports, Manning was his projected No. 1 pick because his "size, athleticism, pocket movement, and willingness to push the ball make for an intriguing package."

Reid pointed out Manning has moments when he looks routine throws look hard and vice versa, adding he has a 9.8 percent off-target rate that ranks 58th among all FBS quarterbacks.

Based on competition so far this season, Manning has had the most difficult slate of opposing defenses among the top quarterbacks.

Per opponent-adjusted efficiency , the Longhorns have faced the seventh-hardest collection of opposing defenses among FBS teams. Mensah and Miami, for comparison, sit at No. 63 in that category.

That could also be used to work against Manning because his numbers in the two highest-profile games Texas has played so far against Ohio State and Tennessee don't look great. He is 37-of-56 (66.1 percent) for 396 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions.

The good news for Manning is he has plenty more opportunities against high-level competition to change the narrative in his favor.

After Saturday's game against unranked Oklahoma, the Longhorns begin a run of five consecutive matchups with teams currently ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll: Florida, Mississippi, Mississippi State, Missouri and LSU.

Manning's college trajectory has been interesting because he has taken the unique path of waiting for his turn at a single institution rather than going through the transfer portal to get on the field right away.

Last season marked Manning's first year as the full-time starter in Texas following two years as a backup. He finished 2025 with 3,163 passing yards, 399 rushing yards and accounted for 36 touchdowns in 13 games.

So far in 2026, Manning has thrown for 862 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions with a 63.5 completion percentage. Texas (4-0) has spent four consecutive weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP poll since its 24-23 win over Ohio State.

articles.title: Mike Ditka - NFL icon, Super Bowl winner and Chicago Bears legend dies aged 86
articles.summary: NFL icon Mike Ditka, who coached the Chicago Bears to the Super Bowl XX title in 1986, dies aged 86.
articles.body:
NFL icon and former Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka has died aged 86.

Ditka coached the Bears to the Super Bowl XX title in 1986 and was the first tight end to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

His family confirmed the news in a statement, but no cause of death was given.

"It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka," said a Ditka family statement.

"While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.

"Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever."

Ditka was the fifth overall pick of the 1961 draft when he joined the Bears as a player and he spent six years with the franchise before spells at the Philadelphia Eagles and the Dallas Cowboys.

He helped the Cowboys win their first Super Bowl in 1972, scoring the final touchdown in a 24-3 win against the Miami Dolphins.

Ditka enjoyed a 12-year playing career, with 427 receptions for 5,812 yards and 43 touchdowns, before retiring at the end of the 1972 season.

He was assistant coach at the Cowboys when they won the 1978 Super Bowl and went on to become Chicago Bears head coach in 1982.

Ditka created a dominant side which had a 15-1 record during the 1985-86 regular season before he led them to victory against the New England Patriots to win Super Bowl XX.

"Mike's impact on the Chicago Bears organisation, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organisation, is immeasurable," said a Bears statement.

"His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations."

Hall of Famer Walter Payton played under Ditka and his son, Jarrett Payton, paid tribute to his father's former coach.

"Da Coach. Hall of Famer. The heartbeat of the '85 Bears and a Super Bowl champion," wrote Payton in a social media post.

articles.title: Social media tributes pour in for former Bears head coach Mike Ditka, who dies at 86
articles.summary: The Hall of Famer had become a beloved icon, thanks to his mustache and the memorable impressions of him, which added humor to his normally stoic demeanor.
articles.body:
Jarrett Payton, son of former Chicago Bears running back Walter Payton, posted that the Ditka family announced Mike Ditka's death Friday morning. He was 86 years old.

Ditka played tight end in the NFL from 1961-72, spending his first six years in Chicago. Over his 12-year career, he caught 427 passes for 5,812 yards and 43 touchdowns, earning 5 Pro Bowl selections. He played two seasons with Philadelphia and played his final four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys.

He returned to the Windy City as head coach in 1982 and coached the Bears for 11 seasons.

The '85 Bears are known as one of the best defenses in NFL history. Ditka led them to a 15-1 record and a Super Bowl XX win over the New England Patriots. It remains the franchise's only Super Bowl win.

Ditka finished his coaching career with a 121-95 record and one Super Bowl title. He was the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, enshrined in the Class of 1988.

Tributes to Ditka, and his impact on the NFL and football overall, poured in on social media.

Ditka attended the University of Pittsburgh from 1958 to 1960. His alma mater honored the former Panther.

Ozzie Guillen paid tribute to Ditka, from one former head coach of a Chicago sports team to another.

While Ditka is known for his tenure as the head coach of the Bears, he ended his coaching career with the New Orleans Saints. He went 15-33 over three seasons with the team from 1997-99.

Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur offered condolences during his Friday press conference. The Packers will face the Bears at Lambeau Field on Sunday in the latest iteration of their historic rivalry.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell learned of Ditka's passing during his press conference. He instantly started regaling the media with a story about Ditka.

Ditka was known for his seriousness on the field and his rants. The head coach pushed that to the side in 2005 as he starred alongside Will Ferrell in "Kicking and Screaming" as the pair played the head coach and assistant coach of a youth soccer team.

Ditka is also the only man to have at least 100 receptions as a player, 100 wins as a head coach, and a Super Bowl win as both player and coach.

Ditka was known for some iconic sayings. Along with the one that Michele Tafoya shouts out below, he was also quoted as saying, "You're never a loser until you quit trying."

Between his coaching stints with the Bears and the Saints, Ditka got into broadcasting. After leaving New Orleans, he returned to broadcasting as a studio analyst for CBS Sports. He also worked for ESPN as a commentator and was known for his radio work.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels to Start for Commanders vs. Giants After Elbow injury Recovery
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will make his return to the lineup on Sunday against the New York Giants, the team announced.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will make his return to the lineup on Sunday against the New York Giants, the team announced.

Offensive coordinator David Blough told reporters Thursday that Daniels was "full go" ahead of the Commanders' Week 5 matchup against the visiting Giants.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Monday he was expecting Daniels to start Sunday.

Daniels was sidelined for two games after suffering his elbow injury Sept. 20 during a Week 2 matchup at the Dallas Cowboys.

The quarterback played just seven games last season in part thanks to recurring issues with his left elbow, which he dislocated in Week 9 of the 2025 campaign.

The Commanders quarterback sat out three games before returning for Week 14. He took 39 more snaps before aggravating the same elbow injury and sitting out the rest of the season.

Commanders general manager Adam Peters said after Daniels' latest left elbow injury the team was not considering surgery or an IR stint for the quarterback.

ESPN's Adam Schefter later reported it sounds like Daniels is "probably" going to need surgery over the offseason but is delaying the procedure in order to remain available this season.

Daniels told reporters Wednesday he considers the brace he will be wearing over his left elbow to be "kind of a part of me now."

He had previously said the brace is different than the version he wore in his Week 14 return last season because it does not allow him to fully extend his left arm.

"I'm gonna embrace it. I'm gonna embrace the brace, not really worry too much about it," Daniels said Wednesday.

The Commanders (1-3) and Giants (3-1) are set to kick off Sunday at 1 p.m. ET in Landover, Maryland.

articles.title: NFL world reacts to death of Bears legend Mike Ditka
articles.summary: The NFL world is reeling following the passing of legendary Bears tight end and coach Mike Ditka.
articles.body:
The NFL world is reeling following the passing of legendary Chicago Bears tight end and Super Bowl-winning head coach Mike Ditka on Friday. Ditka passed away at the age of 86 and leaves behind a legacy as one of the most successful sports figures in Chicago history.

Ditka, who was selected at No. 5 overall in the 1961 NFL draft, spent six seasons with the Bears and helped revolutionize the tight end position as we know it today. In 84 games with Chicago, Ditka totaled 316 receptions for 4,503 yards and 34 touchdowns. He was traded to the Philadelphia Eagles in 1967, where he would go on to play two seasons (1967-68) before spending four years with the Dallas Cowboys (1969-72).

After he retired from playing, Ditka got his coaching start with the Cowboys, serving as an assistant coach under Tom Landry for nine seasons. While working for Dallas, Ditka penned a letter to Bears owner George Halas expressing his desire to return to Chicago and serve as head coach.

The Bears hired Ditka as their head coach in 1982, and he coached the team for 11 seasons. His crowning moment came leading the legendary 1985 Bears to a Super Bowl XX championship, defeating the New England Patriots, 46-10. The '85 Bears had arguably the best defense of all-time and an explosive offense featuring Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton.
