articles.title: Lamar Jackson’s latest injury update doesn’t look good for Ravens
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens is approaching a crucial test, but its preparations raises questions about the availability of its most important player.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens could be heading into one of their most important games of the early season without their biggest offensive weapon. With a primetime matchup against the Atlanta Falcons approaching, Baltimore is still waiting for clarity on the availability of its starting quarterback.

Head coach Jesse Minter has remained hopeful about the situation, leaving the door open for a late decision. However, as the weekend approaches, the Ravens are running out of opportunities to get their franchise quarterback ready for Sunday night.

Lamar Jackson misses another Ravens practice ahead of Falcons game

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8). Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images.

The latest development is concerning: Lamar Jackson was absent during Friday's portion of Ravens practice open to the media, meaning the quarterback has not practiced at all this week while dealing with an ankle injury (h/t Jamison Hensley of ESPN). The continued absence puts his availability for Sunday's game against Atlanta in serious doubt.

Jackson suffered the injury during Baltimore's Week 4 victory over the Tennessee Titans and did not return after halftime. He was later seen leaving the stadium in a protective boot, raising questions about whether he would recover in time for the upcoming matchup.

Despite the missed practices, Minter has not ruled out Jackson playing. The coach said Wednesday that experienced players can sometimes be ready for a game without practicing during the week, adding that the team would continue monitoring Jackson's recovery before making a decision.

Still, missing the entire practice week is hardly encouraging for a quarterback preparing to face a competitive opponent on the road. Until Baltimore provides a definitive update, Jackson's status remains uncertain rather than officially ruled out.

Tyler Huntley could start for Ravens against Falcons

If Jackson cannot play, Tyler Huntley is expected to take over as Baltimore's starting quarterback. The veteran backup replaced Jackson against Tennessee and completed eight of nine passes for 63 yards, while adding 16 rushing yards on four attempts.

Huntley has previous experience stepping in for Jackson, including during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. However, replacing a two-time NFL Most Valuable Player presents a significant challenge, particularly against an Atlanta team that has found momentum after a difficult start to the season.

The Ravens are also managing several other injuries, including issues affecting cornerback Marlon Humphrey and linebacker Trey Hendrickson. Their availability could further complicate Baltimore's preparations for Sunday night.

Baltimore travels to Atlanta for the Week 5 matchup on Sunday, October 11. Jackson's final status will be crucial to the Ravens' game plan, with Huntley preparing to start if the quarterback cannot recover sufficiently to play.

articles.title: Week 5 staff picks: Final score, bold predictions for Saints-Vikings
articles.summary: How do you see this playing out? Here are our Week 5 staff picks, with final scores and bold predictions for New Orleans Saints vs. Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
How do you see this one playing out? The New Orleans Saints (1-3) are desperate for a win after getting embarrassed on Monday Night Football , but they face tough sledding against the Minnesota Vikings (4-0). It's been a short week for the black and gold to recover and get up for this game, but sometimes the only way out is through. Confidence in head coach Kellen Moore is at an all-time low. He's got to get back in the win column, or this thing will just spiral further out of his control.

Here are our staff picks for Week 5, with final scores and bold predictions:

Between a discombobulated Vikings offense and a blitz-heavy Minnesota defense, this might be the lowest-scoring game of the year for New Orleans. The Saints have been shockingly hesitant to leave extra blockers in pass protection, leading to Tyler Shough taking the most hits and third-most sacks in the NFL this season. That's a bad matchup with a Vikings defense that always tries to win the numbers game. Offensively, Minnesota has only averaged 16 points per game since a dominant showing against the Green Bay Packers in Week 1, so this could be a chance for Brandon Staley's battered defense to regain its footing. The question is whether New Orleans can protect Shough. They failed that mission in each of the last two games.

Bold prediction: Chase Young gets two sacks on the afternoon against a Vikings offensive line down several key pieces. -- John Sigler

It goes against all logic with the way the Saints have played at home recently and coming off their Monday night abomination. I'm still sticking with my preseason prediction of a win in this spot over a Vikings squad not nearly as impressive as their record. New Orleans rebounds defensively just enough to force a few key turnovers and puts together their best outing of a so far unimpressive year. It'll be ugly on offense for the Saints in portions against a formidable Viking defense, but New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough again shows the traits of a franchise quarterback.

Bold prediction: New Orleans gets a critical defensive stop late in the fourth quarter. Tyler Shough responds with an impressive game-winning touchdown drive to pull the win out in the final moments with a scoring pass to Chris Olave for the win. -- Bob Rose

Starting the year 1-4 is brutal, but this offensive line has not shown enough to give confidence that they will be able to slow down the Vikings' prolific pass rush. I wouldn't be surprised if this turns into a field goal fest. The Saints defense has to respond and while Minnesota hasn't had the best offense, they have weapons on that offense that will take advantage of the soft approach New Orleans has had on that side of the ball. The Saints have the talent to win the game, it just comes down to preparation and execution. Neither of those have been good enough so far.

Bold prediction: Jonas Sanker gets his first turnover of the season. -- Dylan Sanders

The Saints keep Minnesota's limited offense within reach, but the Vikings' defense ultimately makes the difference. Tyler Shough connects with Olave for several explosive plays before Minnesota forces a late turnover with New Orleans driving to tie the game.

Bold prediction: Chris Olave finishes with more receiving yards than Minnesota records as a team through the air. -- Arye Pulli

With the Saints back at home, I expect them to respond. Brandon Staley's defense should be better prepared to contain a Vikings offense that has struggled to put points on the board, while Tyler Shough and the offense will look to exploit a vulnerable Minnesota secondary. With Chris Olave and company leading the way in the passing game, the Saints have the weapons to make plays downfield and get back on track.

articles.title: From Dyczko to Da Coach: How Mike Ditka became the most Chicago name imaginable
articles.summary: Mike Ditka, 86, was born Dyczko and raised in a Pennsylvania steel town but became Chicago's Da Coach. The city never quit him.
articles.body:
In Thanksgiving week of 2024, Mike Ditka had quietly moved back to Chicago, later putting his Naples, Fla. home up for sale.

"I'm finally home!" Ditka told a Chicago Sun-Times columnist . "This city is my home. I love it."

The grandson of Ukrainian immigrants, Michael Dyczko Jr. was raised in the outskirts of Pittsburgh and became a college star in the city before making it in the National Football League with the Chicago Bears in 1961.

By then the family had long dropped the tougher-to-pronounce Dyczko for the now ubiquitous Ditka, which would eventually belong to his new city. Go figure: An anglicized name to suit a Pennsylvania steel town became a byword for Chicago toughness, a one-word talisman for everything the city believes about itself: stubborn, blue-collar, proud and impossible to ignore.

Walter Payton had the grace, Dick Butkus the menace, Michael Jordan the global sheen. But no name sounds more like the city itself than Ditka: a neighbor, a bartender, an alderman.

The Hammer. Iron Mike. Da Coach. The Great Grabowski.

Ditka went through nicknames the way he went through quarterbacks, and each one fit.

When Ditka's death at the age of 86 was announced by his family Friday morning, it closed the circle on a chapter of Bears history. Ditka was the only person to take part in both of the franchise's last two league championships, as a tight end in 1963 and as the head coach who delivered Super Bowl XX. The Bears haven't won another since.

The Super Bowl made Ditka and the 1985 Bears legends for life in the city whose baseball allegiances might be divided but for whom football is the great connector. He and his team probably haven't paid for a drink in Chicago for 40-plus years because of it.

Ditka's résumé speaks for itself: a Hall of Fame tight end who helped redefine the position, then 106 wins as a head coach, a 15-1 team some consider one of the best ever to be fielded, two Coach of the Year awards and a No. 89 jersey that is the last the Bears have said they'll ever retire.

The Super Bowl made Ditka a household name across the country, fueled by the "Saturday Night Live" skits in his honor that made him something of a beloved caricature of his adopted city. They leaned into every Chicago trope known to man, with mustachioed, beer-and-sausage Bears superfans wearing the Ditka costume – aviator sunglasses, fake 'stache, 80s Bears sweater – predicting future Bears Super Bowls in between cigar puffs and heart-attack scares.

Ditka's own heart attack in 1988 made the gag hit closer to home. He returned from that 11 days later, only ingraining Ditka in Bears fans' hearts even more. Ditka was a good enough sport that he appeared in the SNL superfans skit just days after the Bears had fired him in 1993, chewing his trademark gum into oblivion while doing so.

The premise of the skit was Bill Swerski's superfans writing a protest letter to the Bears over Ditka's firing. But while doing so, the firebrand Ditka also emerged behind the scenes in some hilarious outtakes in which Da Coach turned his ire on da cameraman.

The Bears might have run their course with Ditka by the end of the 1992 season, but Chicago could never quit him. The same stubborn streak that clashed with ownership and finally cost him his job was the one the city loved most: the temper, the plain talk, the refusal to back down. In Ditka, Chicago saw itself.

"I know one thing: I'm a Bear," he once said, and Chicago believed him.

When he came back in 1997 as the head coach of the Saints, beating the Bears in a Sunday night game at Soldier Field that deserves to go down as one of the uglier football games you'll ever experience, Bears fans warmly greeted Ditka – a rarity for opponents. And Da Coach came out on top, 20-17. It was a perfect Ditka moment in Chicago.

He may have lived elsewhere after his Bears days, but Ditka never really left Chicago. The flagship steakhouse that bore his name downtown closed during COVID, but other locations still carry on. Have to imagine business will see an uptick this week. Chicago people still want a piece of Ditka in their lives.

In the end, he wanted a piece of Chicago, too. He moved back in late 2024 and kept a low profile in his final two years as he struggled with his health, but he knew where he belonged.

"It's the people I miss," he told the Sun-Times then, "miss more than anything."

Chicago had kept a place for Da Coach all along.
